title: Helpful to a Fault: Measuring Illicit Assistance in Multi-Turn, Multilingual LLM Agents
summary: LLM-based agents execute real-world workflows via tools and memory. These affordances enable ill-intended adversaries to also use these agents to carry out complex misuse scenarios. Existing agent misuse benchmarks largely test single-prompt instructions, leaving a gap in measuring how agents end up helping with harmful or illegal tasks over multiple turns. We introduce STING (Sequential Testing of Illicit N-step Goal execution), an automated red-teaming framework that constructs a step-by-step illicit plan grounded in a benign persona and iteratively probes a target agent with adaptive follow-ups, using judge agents to track phase completion. We further introduce an analysis framework that models multi-turn red-teaming as a time-to-first-jailbreak random variable, enabling analysis tools like discovery curves, hazard-ratio attribution by attack language, and a new metric: Restricted Mean Jailbreak Discovery. Across AgentHarm scenarios, STING yields substantially higher illicit-task completion than single-turn prompting and chat-oriented multi-turn baselines adapted to tool-using agents. In multilingual evaluations across six non-English settings, we find that attack success and illicit-task completion do not consistently increase in lower-resource languages, diverging from common chatbot findings. Overall, STING provides a practical way to evaluate and stress-test agent misuse in realistic deployment settings, where interactions are inherently multi-turn and often multilingual.

AI.title_translation: 过分乐于助人：测量多轮、多语言LLM智能体中的非法协助行为
AI.tldr: 本文提出了STING自动化红队测试框架，用于评估和度量大语言模型智能体在多轮、多语言交互中协助完成复杂非法任务的风险。
AI.motivation: 现有的智能体滥用基准主要测试单轮提示指令，缺乏衡量智能体如何在多轮交互中最终协助完成有害或非法任务的手段，因此需要一种针对多轮、多语言LLM智能体的实用红队测试和评估方法。
AI.method: 引入STING（Sequential Testing of Illicit N-step Goal execution）自动化红队测试框架，构建基于良性角色的分步非法计划并进行自适应连续探测，同时利用分析框架将多轮红队测试建模为首次越狱时间的随机变量。
AI.result: 在AgentHarm场景下，STING相比单轮提示和聊天导向的多轮基线，能够显著提高非法任务的完成率；在多语言评估中，攻击成功率和非法任务完成率在资源较少的语言中并未一致增加，这与常见聊天机器人的研究结果有所不同。
AI.conclusion: STING框架为评估和压力测试真实部署环境中的智能体滥用提供了一种实用且有效的方法，揭示了多轮交互和多语言设置对智能体安全性的复杂影响。
AI.translation: 基于大语言模型的智能体通过工具和记忆来执行现实世界的 工作流。这些功能使心怀不轨的对手也能够利用这些智能体来实施复杂的滥用场景。现有的智能体滥用基准主要测试单轮提示指令，这在衡量智能体如何在多轮交互中最终协助完成有害或非法任务方面留下了空白。我们介绍了STING（Sequential Testing of Illicit N-step Goal execution），这是一个自动化红队测试框架，它基于良性角色构建逐步的非法计划，并使用自适应的后续跟进迭代探测目标智能体，同时利用裁判智能体来跟踪阶段完成情况。我们进一步引入了一个分析框架，将多轮红队测试建模为首次越狱时间的随机变量，从而启用诸如发现曲线、按攻击语言分类的风险比归因以及一个新指标：受限平均越狱发现等分析工具。在AgentHarm场景中，STING产生了比单轮提示和适应于工具使用智能体的面向聊天的多轮基线更高的非法任务完成率。在六种非英语环境的多语言评估中，我们发现攻击成功率和非法任务完成率在资源较少的语言中并未一致增加，这与常见的聊天机器人研究结果有所不同。总的来说，STING为在现实部署设置中评估和压力测试智能体滥用提供了一种实用方法，其中交互本身具有多轮且通常是多语言的特点。
AI.summary: 该论文介绍了STING，一个用于测量多轮、多语言大语言模型智能体中非法协助行为的自动化红队测试框架。该框架能够通过良性角色构建分步非法计划并进行自适应的多轮探测。实验表明，STING比单轮或传统多轮基线更有效地促使智能体完成非法任务，且在多语言评估中表现出与传统聊天机器人不同的特性。
AI.keywords: 大语言模型智能体, 自动化红队测试, 多轮交互, 多语言评估, 安全性基准
AI.comments: 本文创新性地提出了STING框架，专门针对大语言模型智能体在多轮、多语言交互中的滥用风险进行自动化红队测试，填补了现有智能体滥用评估多限于单轮指令的空白，并在分析中引入了生存分析模型，为理解和度量智能体安全性提供了新的视角和重要工具。

title: Co-Optimization of Network Topology and Variable Impedance Devices under Dynamic Line Ratings in Power Transmission Systems
comments: This paper has been withdrawn due to its similarity to another paper
summary: Power system operators are increasingly deploying Grid Enhancing Technologies (GETs) to mitigate operational challenges such as line and transformer congestion, and voltage violations. These technologies, including Network Topology Optimization (NTO), Variable Impedance Devices (VIDs), and Dynamic Line Rating (DLR), enhance system flexibility and enable better utilization of existing network assets. However, as the deployment of multiple GETs grows, effective coordination among them becomes essential to fully realize their potential benefits. This paper presents a co-optimization framework that models and coordinates NTO, VID, and DLR within a unified optimization scheme to alleviate network congestion and minimize operational costs. The NTO formulation is developed using a node-breaker model, offering finer switching granularity and improved operational flexibility. The inclusion of VIDs introduces nonlinear and non-convex relationships in the optimization problem. DLR takes into account of weather conditions, primarily wind speed and ambient temperature, enabling adaptive utilization of transmission capacity. The proposed framework is validated on standard IEEE benchmark test systems, demonstrating its effectiveness under varying numbers and placements of impedance controllers.
comment: This paper has been withdrawn due to its similarity to another paper

AI.title_translation: 电力输电系统中动态线路容量下网络拓扑与可变阻抗器件的协同优化
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一个将网络拓扑优化、可变阻抗器件和动态线路容量相结合的统一协同优化框架，以缓解电力系统拥塞并降低运行成本。
AI.motivation: 随着多种电网增强技术（GETs）的广泛部署，现有的单一技术应用已难以完全发挥潜力，因此需要有效的协同来缓解输电系统中的线路拥塞、变压器过载和电压越限等操作挑战，并降低运行成本。
AI.method: 提出一个统一的协同优化框架，采用基于节点断路器模型的网络拓扑优化，处理可变阻抗器件引入的非线性非凸关系，并结合基于天气条件的动态线路容量。
AI.result: 在标准的IEEE基准测试系统上进行了验证，结果表明该框架在不同的阻抗控制器数量和布局下均能有效发挥作用。
AI.conclusion: 提出的协同优化框架能够有效缓解电力系统拥塞并最小化运行成本，验证了多电网增强技术联合部署的有效性。
AI.translation: 电力系统运营商越来越多地部署电网增强技术（GETs）来缓解诸如线路和变压器拥塞以及电压越限等运行挑战。这些技术包括网络拓扑优化（NTO）、可变阻抗器件（VIDs）和动态线路容量（DLR），它们增强了系统灵活性并实现了对现有网络资产的更好利用。然而，随着多种GETs部署的增加，它们之间的有效协调对于充分发挥其潜在效益变得至关重要。本文提出了一个协同优化框架，在统一的优化方案中对NTO、VID和DLR进行建模和协调，以缓解网络拥塞并最小化运行成本。NTO公式使用节点断路器模型开发，提供了更精细的开关粒度和更高的运行灵活性。VIDs的引入在优化问题中引入了非线性跟非凸关系。DLR考虑了天气条件（主要是风速和环境温度），从而能够自适应利用输电容量。所提出的框架在标准IEEE基准测试系统上进行了验证，证明了其在不同数量和位置的阻抗控制器下的有效性。
AI.summary: 本文研究了电力输电系统中网络拓扑、可变阻抗器件（VIDs）和动态线路容量（DLR）的协同优化问题。通过建立统一的优化框架，整合了节点断路器模型、非线性阻抗关系以及基于天气的动态容量调整，旨在缓解网络拥塞并降低运行成本，并在IEEE标准算例上验证了其有效性。
AI.keywords: 电网增强技术, 网络拓扑优化, 可变阻抗器件, 动态线路容量, 协同优化
AI.comments: 本文提出了一种针对电力传输系统的网络拓扑、可变阻抗器件和动态线路容量的协同优化框架，创新性地将这三种电网增强技术（GETs）统一建模，并利用IEEE标准算例进行了验证，对提高电网灵活性和降低运行成本具有重要意义。

title: A Cognitive Framework for Idea Diversity in Large Language Models
summary: Consumers, marketers, and new product developers increasingly rely on LLMs for ideation. Yet ideas generated by independent LLM sessions tend to be less diverse than ideas generated by independent samples of humans, raising concerns that widespread reliance on LLMs could homogenize marketplace ideation and decrease consumer welfare. We identify two mechanisms undermining LLM idea diversity, informed by theories of creative ideation from new product development and cognitive psychology. First, LLMs aggregate knowledge into a unified distribution rather than exhibiting the knowledge partitioning inherent to human populations, where each person occupies a distinct region of the knowledge space. Second, at the individual level, LLMs exhibit fixation just as humans do, where early outputs constrain subsequent ideation. Two product-ideation experiments demonstrate that targeted prompting interventions can address both mechanisms. Persona modifiers based on ordinary individuals improve knowledge partitioning but amplify fixation. This fixation can be mitigated by using chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, and combining both strategies produces the highest idea diversity, outperforming humans. These findings offer a theoretically grounded framework for understanding LLM idea diversity and practical strategies for leveraging AI's efficiency without compromising the idea diversity that sustains marketplace variety and consumer welfare.

AI.title_translation: 大型语言模型中创意多样性的认知框架
AI.tldr: 通过结合角色修饰符与思维链提示，可以有效解决大语言模型生成创意时多样性不足的问题，使其创意表现超越人类。
AI.motivation: 当前LLM生成的独立创意多样性低于人类，可能导致市场创意同质化并损害消费者福利，因此需要识别并解决导致LLM创意多样性不足的潜在机制。
AI.method: 基于新产品开发和认知心理学的创意构思理论，识别出LLM创意多样性不足的两个机制，并通过两项产品创意实验，测试了角色修饰符提示和思维链（CoT）提示等针对性干预策略的效果。
AI.result: 实验表明，基于普通人的角色修饰符能改善知识分区但会加剧思维定势；而采用思维链（CoT）提示可以缓解定势；将两者策略相结合能产生最高的主体间和主体内创意多样性，其表现甚至超越人类。
AI.conclusion: 通过将角色修饰符与思维链提示相结合，可以有效克服LLM在知识分布和个体定势上的缺陷，使其生成的创意多样性甚至超越人类，从而在利用AI效率的同时维护市场多样性。
AI.translation: 消费者、营销人员和新产品开发人员越来越多地依赖大型语言模型（LLMs）进行创意构思。然而，独立LLM会话生成的创意往往比人类独立样本生成的创意缺乏多样性，这引发了人们的担忧：广泛依赖LLMs可能会使市场创意同质化并降低消费者福利。根据新产品开发和认知心理学中的创造性构思理论，我们识别出了削弱LLM创意多样性的两个机制。首先，LLMs将知识聚合为一个统一的分布，而不是表现出人类群体所固有的知识分区（其中每个人占据知识空间的独特区域）。其次，在个体层面，LLMs和人类一样表现出定势，即早期输出会限制后续的构思。两项产品创意实验表明，针对性的提示干预可以解决这两个机制。基于普通人的角色修饰符可以改善知识分区，但会加剧定势。通过使用思维链（CoT）提示可以缓解这种定势，而将这两种策略结合起来可以产生最高的创意多样性，甚至优于人类。这些发现为一个理解LLM创意多样性的理论基础框架以及在不损害维持市场多样性和消费者福利的创意多样性的前提下利用AI效率的实用策略提供了支持。
AI.summary: 本文研究了大型语言模型（LLM）在创意生成中多样性不足的问题，指出了其知识聚合和个体思维定势两大机制，并提出结合角色修饰符与思维链提示的干预策略，成功提升了LLM的创意多样性并超越了人类水平。
AI.keywords: 大语言模型, 创意多样性, 认知框架, 知识分区, 思维定势
AI.comments: 该论文从认知心理学和新产品开发的理论出发，深入剖析了大型语言模型（LLM）在创意生成中缺乏多样性的两大根本原因（知识聚合与思维定势），并创新性地提出了通过结合角色修饰符（Persona modifiers）与思维链（CoT）提示词来克服这些缺陷的实用干预策略，具有很高的理论价值和实践指导意义。

title: Same Words, Different Judgments: How Preferences Vary Across Modalities
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track
summary: Preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) is the dominant framework for aligning AI systems to human preferences. However, evaluation protocols for such data were designed for text and have not been validated for speech. We present the first intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)-based, controlled cross-modal study of human and synthetic preference annotations, comparing text and audio evaluations of identical semantic content across 100 prompts. We show that achieving \textit{good} agreement within either modality (ICC(2,$k$) $\approx$ .80) requires $\sim$9 raters and modalities show marked differences in how people report preferences: audio raters exhibit narrower decision thresholds, reduced length bias, and more user-oriented evaluation criteria, with near-chance cross-modality agreement. We demonstrate that synthetic ratings can be used to effectively predict inter-rater agreement, thus serving as an early signal for stimulus selection and proxy for human annotations. Together, these findings argue that evaluation protocols for audio preference data require modality-specific design rather than direct adaptation from text. Code, data, and the audio corpus are available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/sciminds/same-words-different-judgements
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track

AI.title_translation: 相同的词汇，不同的判断：偏好如何在不同模态间变化
AI.tldr: 文本偏好的评估协议不能直接适用于语音，因为人类在文本和音频模态下的偏好判断存在显著差异，需要针对模态进行专门设计。
AI.motivation: 基于偏好的强化学习（PbRL）中，现有的评估协议主要针对文本设计，未经验证是否适用于语音模态，因此需要探究人类偏好在不同模态间的差异。
AI.method: 开展了基于组内相关系数（ICC）的控制变量交叉模态研究，比较了100个相同语义提示下的文本和音频评估，涉及人类和合成偏好标注。
AI.result: 在任一模态下达到良好一致性（ICC $\approx$ 0.80）均需约9名评分者；音频评分者具有更窄的决策阈值、更低的长度偏差以及更以用户为中心的标准，跨模态一致性接近随机水平；同时证明合成评分可有效预测评分者间的一致性。
AI.conclusion: 音频偏好数据不能直接套用文本的评估协议，必须进行模态特定设计，且合成评分可作为预测评分者间一致性的有效代理。
AI.translation: 基于偏好的强化学习（PbRL）是对齐AI系统与人类偏好的主流框架。然而，此类数据的评估协议是为文本设计的，尚未在语音中得到验证。我们提出了首个基于组内相关系数（ICC）的人类与合成偏好标注的控制交叉模态研究，在100个提示词中比较了相同语义内容的文本和音频评估。我们表明，在任一模态中实现“良好”的一致性（ICC(2,$k$) $\approx$ .80）都需要约9名评分者，并且模态在人们如何报告偏好方面表现出显著差异：音频评分者表现出更窄的决策阈值、减少的长度偏差和更多以用户为中心的评估标准，跨模态一致性接近随机水平。我们证明，合成评分可以有效地用于预测评分者间的一致性，从而作为刺激选择的早期信号和人类标注的代理。总之，这些发现表明，音频偏好数据的评估协议需要针对模态进行特定设计，而不是直接从文本调整。代码、数据和音频语料库可在以下网址获取：https://huggingface.co/datasets/sciminds/same-words-different-judgements
AI.summary: 本文通过一项基于ICC的控制变量跨模态研究，比较了文本和音频在相同语义内容下的偏好标注，发现两种模态在人类偏好判断上存在显著差异（如决策阈值、长度偏差和评估标准不同），跨模态一致性接近随机水平，从而证明语音偏好数据需要专门的评估协议。
AI.keywords: 偏好强化学习, 跨模态研究, 语音评估, 一致性检验, 合成评分
AI.comments: 该研究首次对文本和语音模态下的人类与合成偏好标注进行了控制变量交叉模态研究，揭示了不同模态下人类偏好判断的显著差异，强调了语音偏好数据需要量身定制的评估协议，具有重要的理论和实践意义。

title: MuonRec: Shifting the Optimizer Paradigm Beyond Adam in Scalable Generative Recommendation
comments: The article has been accepted by Frontiers of Computer Science (FCS), with the DOI: {10.1007/s11704-026-61514-9}
summary: Recommender systems (RecSys) are increasingly emphasizing scaling, leveraging larger architectures and more interaction data to improve personalization. Yet, despite the optimizer's pivotal role in training, modern RecSys pipelines almost universally default to Adam/AdamW, with limited scrutiny of whether these choices are truly optimal for recommendation. In this work, we revisit optimizer design for scalable recommendation and introduce MuonRec, the first framework that brings the recently proposed Muon optimizer to RecSys training. Muon performs orthogonalized momentum updates for 2D weight matrices via Newton-Schulz iteration, promoting diverse update directions and improving optimization efficiency. We develop an open-source training recipe for recommendation models and evaluate it across both traditional sequential recommenders and modern generative recommenders. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MuonRec reduces converged training steps by an average of 32.4\% while simultaneously improving final ranking quality. Specifically, MuonRec yields consistent relative gains in NDCG@10, averaging 12.6\% across all settings, with particularly pronounced improvements in generative recommendation models. These results consistently outperform strong Adam/AdamW baselines, positioning Muon as a promising new optimizer standard for RecSys training. Our code is available.
comment: The article has been accepted by Frontiers of Computer Science (FCS), with the DOI: {10.1007/s11704-026-61514-9}

AI.title_translation: MuonRec：在可扩展生成式推荐中将优化器范式推向Adam之外
AI.tldr: MuonRec是首个将Muon优化器引入推荐系统的框架，通过正交化动量更新，在减少32.4%训练步数的同时显著提升了生成式推荐模型的性能。
AI.motivation: 现代推荐系统普遍默认采用Adam/AdamW优化器，缺乏对大规模可扩展推荐模型而言这些选择是否最优的审视，因此需要重新审视并设计适用于可扩展推荐的优化器范式。
AI.method: 引入Muon优化器，通过牛顿-舒尔茨迭代（Newton-Schulz iteration）对二维权重矩阵进行正交化动量更新，并开发了针对推荐模型的开源训练配方。
AI.result: 实验表明，MuonRec平均减少了32.4%的收敛训练步数，同时最终排序质量（NDCG@10）在各种设置下平均提升了12.6%，在生成式推荐模型中表现尤为突出。
AI.conclusion: MuonRec作为一种新颖的推荐系统优化器框架，显著提高了大规模推荐模型的训练效率和最终性能，有望取代Adam/AdamW成为推荐系统训练的新标准。
AI.translation: 推荐系统（RecSys）越来越强调规模化，利用更大的架构和更多的交互数据来改善个性化。然而，尽管优化器在训练中起着关键作用，现代RecSys流水线几乎普遍默认采用Adam/AdamW，对这些选择是否真正最适合推荐的审视却很有限。在这项工作中，我们重新审视了可扩展推荐的优化器设计，并推出了MuonRec，这是第一个将最近提出的Muon优化器引入RecSys训练的框架。Muon通过牛顿-舒尔茨迭代对2D权重矩阵执行正交化动量更新，促进了多样化的更新方向并提高了优化效率。我们为推荐模型开发了一个开源训练配方，并在传统序列推荐器和现代生成式推荐器中进行了评估。大量实验表明，MuonRec在将收敛训练步数平均减少32.4%的同时，还改善了最终的排序质量。具体而言，MuonRec在所有设置下都使NDCG@10获得了持续的相对增益，平均达到12.6%，在生成式推荐模型中的改进尤为显著。这些结果始终优于强Adam/AdamW基线，将Muon定位为RecSys训练的一个有前景的新优化器标准。我们的代码已开源。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了MuonRec，这是首个将Muon优化器引入可扩展推荐系统（RecSys）训练的框架。通过对2D权重矩阵执行正交化动量更新，MuonRec显著提升了优化效率，减少了32.4%的训练步数，并在各种基准测试中将NDCG@10平均提升了12.6%，超越了传统的Adam/AdamW优化器。
AI.keywords: 推荐系统, 优化器, Muon, 生成式推荐, 深度学习训练
AI.comments: 该论文首次将Muon优化器引入推荐系统领域，打破了Adam/AdamW在可扩展推荐模型训练中的垄断地位。通过正交化动量更新，在减少训练步数的同时显著提升了推荐排序指标（如NDCG@10），为推荐系统特别是生成式推荐的高效训练提供了新范式。

title: Evaluation of Visual Processing Should Be Human-Centered, Not Metric-Centered
summary: This position paper argues that the evaluation of modern visual processing systems should no longer be driven primarily by single-metric image quality assessment benchmarks, particularly in the era of generative and perception-oriented methods. Image restoration exemplifies this divergence: while objective IQA metrics enable reproducible, scalable evaluation, they have increasingly drifted apart from human perception and user preferences. We contend that this mismatch risks constraining innovation and misguiding research progress across visual processing tasks. Rather than rejecting metrics altogether, this paper calls for a rebalancing of evaluation paradigms, advocating a more human-centered, context-aware, and fine-grained approach to assessing the visual models' outcomes.

AI.title_translation: 视觉处理的评估应当以人为中心，而非以指标为中心
AI.tldr: 现代视觉处理系统的评估不应再由单一指标主导，而应转向以人类感知和用户偏好为中心的评估范式。
AI.motivation: 现代视觉处理系统（特别是生成式和面向感知的方法）的评估主要依赖单一的图像质量评估基准，这与人类感知和用户偏好日益脱节，从而可能限制创新并误导研究方向。
AI.method: 论文提出了立场观点，通过分析图像恢复等领域的现状，指出客观指标与人类感知的偏差，并呼吁重新平衡评估范式。
AI.result: 指出当前指标驱动评估的局限性并倡导建立一种更贴近人类感知、情境感知和细粒度的评估方法，以纠正传统指标与真实用户偏好之间的偏差。
AI.conclusion: 视觉处理系统的评估必须从单一的、以指标为中心的模式转向以人类为中心、情境感知和细粒度的评估范式。
AI.translation: 这篇立场论文认为，现代视觉处理系统的评估不应再主要由单一指标的图像质量评估基准驱动，特别是在生成式和面向感知的方法时代。图像恢复体现了这种分歧：虽然客观的图像质量评估（IQA）指标能够实现可重复、可扩展的评估，但它们与人类感知和用户偏好的差距却越来越大。我们认为，这种错位可能会限制创新并误导各个视觉处理任务的研究进展。本文并非完全拒绝指标，而是呼吁重新平衡评估范式，倡导采用更以人类为中心、具有情境感知和细粒度的方法来评估视觉模型的结果。
AI.summary: 本文是一篇立场论文，批评了现代视觉处理系统过度依赖单一指标图像质量评估的现状，指出其与人类感知存在脱节，并呼吁建立更具情境感知和以人为本的评估新范式。
AI.keywords: 视觉处理系统, 图像质量评估, 以人为中心, 生成式方法, 评估范式
AI.comments: 这篇立场论文指出了当前视觉处理系统评估中的核心痛点：传统客观指标与人类主观感知严重脱节。强调以人为中心的评估方式对于生成式和面向感知的方法至关重要，对未来的研究导向具有重要的修正意义。

title: Universal Conceptual Structure in Neural Translation: Probing NLLB-200's Multilingual Geometry
comments: 32 pages, 16 figures, 1 summary table; v2 adds non-linear mutual k-NN, ABTT D=1..10, Participation Ratio, LDND Mantel, ANCOVA frequency/fertility controls, and interactive companion at https://kylemath.github.io/InterpretCognates/ ; code at https://github.com/kylemath/InterpretCognates
summary: Do multilingual translation models organize meaning around a shared conceptual space, or do they primarily encode language identity and surface form? We probe the encoder geometry of Meta's 600M-parameter NLLB-200 model across 135 languages and 101 Swadesh concepts in contextualized carrier-frame and decontextualized bare-word regimes against null and confound controls. First, two-way variance partitioning reveals an additive language-shift plus conceptual-manifold geometry: language shifts account for 45.7% of variance on bare words vs. 13.7% in context, and mean-centering improves the between-to-within-concept distance ratio (vs. a 0.99 permutation null) by 2.14x on bare words (1.15 to 2.46; 2.27x across disjoint scripts) and 1.19x in context (2.25 to 2.69), with conceptual separation peaking at Layer 10 (mutual k-NN overlap jumping 4.35x). Second, semantic category explains 25.4% of Swadesh convergence variance ($F(7,93)=4.53$, $p=2.21\times 10^{-4}$; partial $F=7.74$ controlling for fertility and length)---over 20x orthography or phonology ($R^2\le 0.012$)---while the advantage of Swadesh over non-loanword concrete nouns ($d=0.54$--$0.69$) is mediated by Zipfian subword compactness ($p=7.43\times 10^{-7}$). Third, language distances track ASJP NLD and LDND phonetic distances within subfamilies under block-permutation and cross-script controls ($ρ_s=0.65$--$0.67$, block $p=10^{-4}$; global bare-word Mantel $ρ_s=0.24$, $p=0.001$), and CLICS$^3$ colexified concepts lie closer across string-distinct, within-category ($ρ_s=0.32$), and bare-word ($d=1.79$) controls ($d=1.43$, $p=1.55\times 10^{-33}$). Finally, basic color terms recover the Berlin and Kay hierarchy ($ρ_s=0.91$--$0.93$, $p\le 2.18\times 10^{-4}$), and semantic offsets exceed distance-matched controls ($p=3.55\times 10^{-5}$, $d=1.06$). We release InterpretCognates, an interactive toolkit and reproducible suite.
comment: 32 pages, 16 figures, 1 summary table; v2 adds non-linear mutual k-NN, ABTT D=1..10, Participation Ratio, LDND Mantel, ANCOVA frequency/fertility controls, and interactive companion at https://kylemath.github.io/InterpretCognates/ ; code at https://github.com/kylemath/InterpretCognates

AI.title_translation: 神经翻译中的通用概念结构：探究NLLB-200的多语言几何学
AI.tldr: 大型多语言翻译模型NLLB-200的底层编码器展现出共享的概念流形与加性语言偏移并存的几何结构，证明了其组织了通用的概念空间。
AI.motivation: 探究多语言翻译模型究竟是围绕一个共享的 conceptual space（概念空间）来组织语义，还是主要编码语言的身份和表层形式。
AI.method: 使用NLLB-200模型，在135种语言和101个Swadesh概念下，采用上下文语境与去上下文裸词机制，通过双向方差划分、置换零假设控制、均值中心化、语义类别回归以及与人类语言学距离（ASJP等）的对比来探究编码器几何。
AI.result: 研究发现：1. 呈现出加性语言偏移加上概念流形的几何结构，概念分离在第10层达到峰值；2. 语义类别对Swadesh收敛方差的解释力远超正字法或音系学；3. 语言距离可追踪语系内的语音距离；4. 基本颜色词恢复了Berlin和Kay等级体系。
AI.conclusion: NLLB-200编码器展现出了一个由加性语言偏移和共享概念流形共同组成的通用概念结构，证明了大型多语言模型确实在底层组织了一个超越语言界限的共享概念空间。
AI.translation: 多语言翻译模型是围绕共享的概念空间来组织意义，还是主要编码语言身份和表层形式？我们针对Meta的6亿参数NLLB-200模型，在135种语言和101个Swadesh概念（涵盖上下文承载框架和去上下文裸词机制，并结合零假设和混淆控制）下，探测了其编码器几何结构。首先，双向方差划分揭示了“加性语言偏移外加概念流形”的几何结构：在裸词上，语言偏移占方差的45.7%（在上下文中为13.7%），均值中心化使类间与类内距离比提高了2.14倍（裸词：从1.15到2.46；跨不相交脚本为2.27倍），在上下文中提高了1.19倍（从2.25到2.69），概念分离在第10层达到峰值（互k-NN重叠跃升4.35倍）。其次，语义类别解释了Swadesh收敛方差的25.4%，超过正字法或音系学的20倍以上（$R^2\le 0.012$），而Swadesh相比非借词具体名词的优势受Zipfian子词紧凑性的调节。第三，语言距离在区组置换和跨脚本控制下追踪了子家族内的ASJP NLD和LDND语音距离，且CLICS$^3$共义概念在各种控制下距离更近。最后，基本颜色词恢复了Berlin和Kay等级体系，语义偏移超过了距离匹配的对照组。我们发布了InterpretCognates交互式工具包和可复现套件。
AI.summary: 该论文通过探测Meta的NLLB-200模型在135种语言和101个概念上的几何结构，证明了该模型构建了一个由加性语言偏移和共享概念流形组成的通用概念结构，揭示了神经网络中多语言语义组织的底层规律。
AI.keywords: 多语言机器翻译, 概念结构, 编码器几何, 语义对齐, NLLB-200
AI.comments: 该论文深入探讨了大规模多语言机器翻译模型NLLB-200底层的几何结构，首次以庞大的语言和概念规模证实了共享概念流形与语言偏移叠加存在的特性，对理解神经网络中的多语言语义对齐具有重要意义。

title: Complete Diagrammatic Axiomatisations of Relative Entropy
comments: Final proceedings version for MFPS XLII
summary: Relative entropy is a fundamental class of distances between probability distributions, with widespread applications in probability theory, statistics, and machine learning. In this work, we study relative entropy from a categorical perspective, viewing it as a quantitative enrichment of categories of stochastic matrices. We consider two natural monoidal structures on stochastic matrices, given by the Kronecker product and the direct sum. Our main results are complete axiomatisations of Kullback-Leibler divergence and, more generally, of Rényi divergences of arbitrary order, for each such structure. Our axiomatic theories are formulated within the framework of quantitative monoidal algebra, using a graphical language of string diagrams enriched with quantitative equations.
comment: Final proceedings version for MFPS XLII

AI.title_translation: 相对熵的完整图解公理化
AI.tldr: 本文利用图解语言和定量单oidal代数，首次给出了KL散度和Rényi散度的完整公理化体系。
AI.motivation: 相对熵是概率论、统计学和机器学习中的基础距离概念，但缺乏基于图解语言的完整公理化刻画。本文旨在从范畴论和定量单oidal代数出发，填补这一空白。
AI.method: 采用范畴论视角，将相对熵视为随机矩阵范畴的定量富集，在定量单oidal代数框架内，利用带有定量方程的弦图语言进行研究。
AI.result: 给出了Kullback-Leibler散度以及更一般的任意阶Rényi散度在Kronecker积和直和这两种自然单oidal结构下的完整公理化。
AI.conclusion: 本文成功为随机矩阵范畴中的相对熵（包括KL散度和任意阶Rényi散度）建立了完整的图解公理化体系，丰富了定量单oidal代数的研究。
AI.translation: 相对熵是概率分布之间的一类基础距离，在概率论、统计学和机器学习中有着广泛的应用。在这项工作中，我们从范畴论的角度研究相对熵，将其视为随机矩阵范畴的定量富集。我们考虑了随机矩阵上的两种自然单oidal结构，即Kronecker积和直和。我们的主要结果是针对每种结构，对Kullback-Leibler散度以及更一般的任意阶Rényi散度给出了完整的公理化。我们的公理化理论是在定量单oidal代数的框架内制定的，使用了富含定量方程的弦图图形语言。
AI.summary: 本文从范畴论和定量单oidal代数出发，研究了概率分布间的相对熵。通过将随机矩阵的范畴视为定量富集，并利用带有定量方程的弦图语言，作者成功给出了Kullback-Leibler散度以及任意阶Rényi散度在Kronecker积和直和结构下的完整图解公理化。
AI.keywords: 相对熵, 范畴论, 图解公理化, Kullback-Leibler散度, Rényi散度
AI.comments: 该论文从范畴论和定量单oidal代数的全新视角出发，利用弦图语言给出了相对熵（KL散度和Rényi散度）的完整图解公理化，为概率论、统计学和机器学习中的基础度量提供了坚实的代数基础。

title: vLLM Hook v1: A Plug-in for Programming Model Internals on vLLM
summary: Modern artificial intelligence models are deployed on inference engines to optimize runtime efficiency and resource allocation, particularly for transformer-based large language models. The vLLM project is a major open-source library to support model serving and inference. However, the current implementation of vLLM limits programmability of the internal states of deployed models. This prevents the use of popular test-time model alignment and enhancement methods. For example, it prevents the detection of adversarial prompts based on attention patterns or the adjustment of model responses based on activation steering. To bridge this critical gap, we present vLLM Hook, an opensource plug-in to enable the programming of internal states for vLLM models. Based on a configuration file specifying which internal states to capture, vLLM Hook provides seamless integration to vLLM and supports two essential features: passive programming and active programming. For passive programming, vLLM Hook probes the selected internal states for subsequent analysis, while keeping the model generation intact. For active programming, vLLM Hook enables efficient intervention of model generation by altering the selected internal states. In version 1 (named vLLM Hook MIA), the plugin runs on vLLM's V2 model runner and preserves the engine's CUDA graphs, so that capturing and steering internal states incurs only a small decoding overhead. It supports both offline use and serving through vllm serve. In addition to presenting the core functions of vLLM Hook, we demonstrate use cases including prompt injection detection, attention-based re-ranking for retrieval-augmented generation, activation steering, hidden-state probing, hallucination detection, schema linking for text-to-SQL, and tool-call risk assessment. Finally, we welcome the community's contribution to improve vLLM Hook via https://github.com/IBM/vLLM-Hook.

AI.title_translation: vLLM Hook v1：一个在vLLM上编程模型内部机制的插件
AI.tldr: vLLM Hook是一个为vLLM打造的开源插件，能够以极低开销对大模型的内部状态进行高效的捕获和主动干预。
AI.motivation: 当前的vLLM实现限制了对部署模型内部状态的可编程性，从而妨碍了测试时模型对齐、对抗提示词检测以及激活引导等流行方法的应用。
AI.method: 开发了开源插件vLLM Hook（v1版运行于vLLM的V2模型 runner），利用配置文件指定内部状态捕获，支持被动编程（探测状态）和主动编程（干预状态），并保留了引擎的CUDA graphs以维持高性能。
AI.result: vLLM Hook实现了捕获和引导内部状态仅产生很小的解码开销，支持离线使用和`vllm serve`在线服务，并成功演示了提示词注入检测、激活引导、幻觉检测等多个用例。
AI.conclusion: vLLM Hook v1成功弥补了vLLM在内部状态可编程性上的空白，通过提供被动和主动编程功能，在保持高性能的同时扩展了vLLM的应用场景。
AI.translation: 现代人工智能模型被部署在推理引擎上以优化运行效率和资源分配，特别是对于基于Transformer的大型语言模型。vLLM项目是支持模型服务和推理的主要开源库。然而，当前vLLM的实现限制了对部署模型内部状态的可编程性。这阻碍了流行测试时模型对齐和增强方法的使用。例如，它阻止了基于注意力模式的对抗性提示词检测或基于激活引导的模型响应调整。为了弥补这一关键差距，我们提出了vLLM Hook，这是一个开源插件，用于实现vLLM模型的内部状态编程。基于指定要捕获哪些内部状态的配置文件，vLLM Hook提供了与vLLM的无缝集成，并支持两个基本功能：被动编程和主动编程。对于被动编程，vLLM Hook探测选定的内部状态以供后续分析，同时保持模型生成完整。对于主动编程，vLLM Hook通过改变选定的内部状态来实现对模型生成的有效干预。在版本1（名为vLLM Hook MIA）中，该插件在vLLM的V2模型运行器上运行，并保留了引擎的CUDA图，因此捕获和引导内部状态仅产生很小的解码开销。它支持离线使用和通过vllm serve提供服务。除了介绍vLLM Hook的核心功能外，我们还演示了用例，包括提示词注入检测、基于检索增强生成的注意力重排序、激活引导、隐藏状态探测、幻觉检测、文本到SQL的模式链接以及工具调用风险评估。最后，我们欢迎社区通过https://github.com/IBM/vLLM-Hook贡献力量以改进vLLM Hook。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了vLLM Hook v1，这是一个专为vLLM设计的开源插件，旨在解决模型内部状态可编程性不足的问题。它通过配置文件支持被动探测和主动干预模型的内部状态，同时保留了CUDA图优化以确保低开销，并广泛适用于各种大模型的增强与安全任务。
AI.keywords: vLLM, 大语言模型, 模型内部状态, 激活引导, 推理引擎
AI.comments: 该论文针对vLLM推理引擎无法灵活修改模型内部状态的问题，提出了vLLM Hook插件。其创新之处在于通过支持被动和主动编程，在保留CUDA图优化的前提下，以极小的解码开销实现了对模型内部状态的高效捕获与干预，为测试时对齐、幻觉检测等高级应用提供了重要支撑。

title: EmbedTalk: Talking Head Synthesis using Gaussian Embeddings
summary: Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a popular method for real-time talking head synthesis, offering high-quality renderings at low latency. Tri-planes are a common choice for encoding Gaussians prior to deformation since they provide a compact and continuous representation. However, tri-plane encodings are limited by grid resolution and approximation errors introduced by projecting 3D volumetric fields onto 2D subspaces. Recent work has demonstrated the effectiveness of per-Gaussian embeddings for driving temporal deformations in 4D scene reconstruction. We introduce EmbedTalk, which leverages these embeddings to model speech-driven facial deformations for talking head synthesis. Comprehensive experiments show that EmbedTalk improves rendering quality, lip synchronisation, and motion consistency over previous 3DGS-based methods, while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art generative models. Replacing tri-plane features with embeddings also yields significantly more compact models that achieve 60+ FPS on a laptop GPU (RTX 2060 6 GB). Code and further details are available at https://arpita2512.github.io/EmbedTalk/

AI.title_translation: EmbedTalk：使用高斯嵌入的说话人脸合成
AI.tldr: EmbedTalk 通过使用高斯嵌入代替三平面编码，实现了更高质量、更好唇语同步以及在笔记本 GPU 上运行超过 60 FPS 的实时说话人脸合成。
AI.motivation: 现有的基于可变形 3D 高斯泼溅（3DGS）的说话人脸合成方法多采用三平面（tri-plane）来编码高斯参数，但三平面编码受到网格分辨率和 3D 体积场投影到 2D 子空间时产生的近似误差的限制；同时为了利用 per-Gaussian embeddings 在 4D 场景重建中驱动时间形变的优势，需要将其引入到语音驱动的说话人脸合成中。
AI.method: 引入名为 EmbedTalk 的方法，利用 per-Gaussian embeddings（每个高斯点的嵌入）来直接建模语音驱动的面部形变，从而避开了三平面编码在 3D 到 2D 投影中的网格分辨率限制与近似误差。
AI.result: 综合实验表明，EmbedTalk 在渲染质量、唇语同步以及运动一致性方面均优于以往基于 3DGS 的方法，并与最先进的生成模型具有竞争力；此外，模型更加紧凑，在笔记本 GPU (RTX 2060 6 GB) 上可实现 60+ FPS 的实时渲染。
AI.conclusion: EmbedTalk 成功利用高斯嵌入取代了传统的三平面编码，实现了高质量、高效率的语音驱动实时说话人脸合成，并在模型紧凑性和渲染帧率上取得了显著突破。
AI.translation: 可变形三维高斯泼溅（3DGS）已成为实时说话人脸合成的一种流行方法，它以低延迟提供了高质量的渲染效果。三平面是变形前编码高斯函数的常见选择，因为它们提供了一种紧凑且连续的表示。然而，三平面编码受到网格分辨率以及将 3D 体积场投影到 2D 子空间所引入的近似误差的限制。最近的研究证明了每个高斯点的嵌入（per-Gaussian embeddings）在驱动 4D 场景重建中的时间形变方面的有效性。我们介绍了 EmbedTalk，它利用这些嵌入来建模用于说话人脸合成的语音驱动面部形变。综合实验表明，与以往基于 3DGS 的方法相比，EmbedTalk 改善了渲染质量、唇语同步和运动一致性，同时与最先进的生成模型保持竞争力。用嵌入替换三平面特征还产生了明显更紧凑的模型，在笔记本 GPU（RTX 2060 6 GB）上实现了 60+ FPS 的帧率。代码和更多详情可在 https://arpita2512.github.io/EmbedTalk/ 获取。
AI.summary: EmbedTalk 是一种新型的语音驱动说话人脸合成方法，它利用高斯嵌入代替传统的三平面编码来建模面部形变，从而克服了分辨率和投影误差的限制，实现了更高质量、更具动感一致性且运行帧率超过 60 FPS 的实时轻量化渲染。
AI.keywords: 3D Gaussian Splatting, 说话人脸合成, 高斯嵌入, 实时渲染, 语音驱动面部形变
AI.comments: EmbedTalk 通过放弃传统的三平面（tri-plane）编码转而采用高斯嵌入（Gaussian embeddings），有效解决了三平面由于网格分辨率和投影误差带来的瓶颈。该方法不仅提升了渲染质量、唇语同步和运动一致性，还实现了模型轻量化和极高的运行帧率（在笔记本 GPU 上超过 60 FPS），展现出极强的实用价值和前沿创新性。

title: SMAT: Staged Multi-Agent Training for Co-Adaptive Exoskeleton Control
comments: Accepted to IROS 2026. 8 pages, 7 figures. v2: camera-ready version; added code link and funding acknowledgment; clarified method details and limitations
summary: Effective exoskeleton assistance requires co-adaptation: as the device alters joint dynamics, the user reorganizes neuromuscular coordination, creating a non-stationary learning problem. Most learning-based approaches do not explicitly account for the sequential nature of human motor adaptation, leading to training instability and poorly timed assistance. We propose Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT), a four-stage curriculum inspired by how users acclimate to a wearable device. In SMAT, a musculoskeletal human actor and a bilateral hip exoskeleton actor are trained progressively: the human first learns unassisted gait, then adapts to the added device mass; the exoskeleton subsequently learns a positive assistance pattern against a stabilized human policy, and finally both agents co-adapt with full torque capacity and bidirectional feedback. We implement SMAT in the MyoAssist simulation environment using a 26-muscle lower-limb model and an attached hip exoskeleton. Our musculoskeletal simulations demonstrate that the learned exoskeleton control policy produces an average 10.1% reduction in simulated hip muscle activation relative to the no-assist condition. We validated the learned controller in an offline setting using open-source gait data, then deployed it to a physical hip exoskeleton for treadmill experiments with five subjects. The resulting policy delivers consistent assistance and predominantly positive mechanical power without the need for any explicitly imposed timing shift (mean positive power: 13.6 W at 6 Nm RMS torque to 23.8 W at 9.3 Nm RMS torque, with minimal negative power) consistently across all subjects without subject-specific retraining.

title: Truth as a Compression Artifact in Language Model Training
comments: v4: 30 pages, 2 figures. Revised evaluation using probability mass over the full false support; added negative controls and learnable-selector experiments up to 3.08B parameters. Updated claims and discussion
summary: When a transformer is trained from scratch on corpora that solve the same mathematical problem both correctly and incorrectly, which solution does it prefer? The usual test is pairwise, and it is not neutral: when the error can take several forms, a model that merely reproduces training frequencies wins it without preferring anything. We instead score the correct completion against every string the error generator can produce, a share on which frequency matching scores exactly 0.500. At 86M parameters the correct completion holds 59.0% +/- 0.8% of the mass against random errors (59.4% on an independent corpus), where the single realized error gives 77.6% and pair accuracy 87.4%, a three- to fourfold overstatement of the excess above chance; below 86M the primary corpus shows no preference. The coherent false rules of the main corpora are not filtered at any size (43.5--48.8%; the shortfall below 0.5 is a completion-length effect). Two experiments built to identify a compression mechanism raise the pairwise measures while the summed share stays flat or falls: both are negative controls, and compression remains motivation, not a measured mechanism. With the scored false strings held fixed, a false rule whose selector the model can learn moves the correct share from 5 points above the null to 7 below (418M--3.08B), though the correct completion still outweighs the selected string. What these models leave unfiltered is consistent or learnable false structure (one single-rule corruption excepted), not falsehood as such.

title: Ethical Fairness in Ubiquitous Health Sensing without Known Attributes
summary:
Wearable and mobile sensing models infer health and well-being in everyday life, yet strong average performance can conceal failures for particular people, contexts, or devices. Existing fairness methods often require sensitive attributes during training, although such attributes may be unavailable, privacy-sensitive, or restricted. Moreover, they may reduce disparities by degrading performance for some subgroups, violating the ethical principle of non-maleficence.
  We present FLARE (Fisher-guided LAtent-subgroup learning with do-no-harm REgularization), to our knowledge the first attribute-free framework to operationalize beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice in ubiquitous sensing. FLARE uses Fisher information to regularize loss curvature and combines representation, loss, and curvature signals to discover latent performance strata. It then trains a separate model for each stratum using do-no-harm regularization and validation-controlled parameter sharing. We also introduce BHE (Benefit, Harm-Avoidance, Equity), a metric suite for evaluating ethical fairness beyond statistical parity. Across four physiological, behavioral, and clinical sensing datasets, FLARE achieves the highest mean subgroup F1 on every dataset. It is the only evaluated method that improves mean subgroup performance without degrading any evaluated subgroup and the only one that reduces disparity across all 15 evaluated sensitive attributes. Although some baselines achieve larger average disparity reductions, each harms at least one subgroup. Post-hoc analyses on two datasets show that the discovered strata are only weakly aligned with recorded attributes and identify a recurrent within-person state that participant-level attributes cannot capture. Label-free routing and inference take at most 8.1 ms per sample on a smartphone and 10.5 ms on a Raspberry Pi, supporting real-time on-device deployment.

title: An Alternative Trajectory for Generative AI
summary:
The generative artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem is undergoing rapid transformations that threaten its sustainability. As models transition from research prototypes to high-traffic products, the energetic burden has shifted from one-time training to recurring, unbounded inference. This is exacerbated by reasoning models that inflate compute costs by orders of magnitude per query. The prevailing pursuit of artificial general intelligence through scaling of monolithic models is colliding with hard physical constraints: grid failures, water consumption, and diminishing returns on data scaling. This trajectory yields models with impressive factual recall but struggles in domains requiring in-depth reasoning, possibly due to insufficient abstractions in training data.
  Current large language models (LLMs) exhibit genuine reasoning depth only in domains like mathematics and coding, where rigorous, pre-existing abstractions provide structural grounding. In other fields, the current approach fails to generalize well. We propose an alternative trajectory based on domain-specific superintelligence (DSS). We argue for first constructing explicit symbolic abstractions (knowledge graphs, ontologies, and formal logic) to underpin synthetic curricula enabling small language models to master domain-specific reasoning without the model collapse problem typical of LLM-based synthetic data methods.
  Rather than a single generalist giant model, we envision "societies of DSS models": dynamic ecosystems where orchestration agents route tasks to distinct DSS back-ends. This paradigm shift decouples capability from size, enabling intelligence to migrate from energy-intensive data centers to secure, on-device experts. By aligning algorithmic progress with physical constraints, DSS societies move generative AI from an environmental liability to a sustainable force for economic empowerment.

title: A Unified Pulse-Shaped OFDM Framework for Chirp-Domain Waveforms: Continuous-Time Modeling and Practical I/O Analysis
comments: 14 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications. The supplementary materials for this paper are available at: https://oddm.io
summary: A unified framework for chirp-domain waveforms, including orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) and affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM), is developed. Their continuous-time representations are shown to fall within the conventional Weyl-Heisenberg (WH) framework for multicarrier waveforms, with the root chirp as the prototype pulse. Since the root chirp has constant envelope and is transparent to subcarrier orthogonality, these waveforms can be further interpreted as pulse-shaped (PS) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, whose power spectral density is derived analytically. The derived spectrum reveals that implementations based on the discrete affine Fourier transform rely on sub-Nyquist samples and exhibit frequency aliasing. We prove that the corresponding aliased chirps are only conditionally orthogonal, whereas sample-wise root-Nyquist pulse shaping of the discrete-time AFDM (DT-AFDM) sequence produces mutually orthogonal pulse-shaped chirps, resulting in the pulse-shaped AFDM (PS-AFDM) waveform. We then derive an exact waveform-level input-output (I/O) relation for PS-AFDM over delay-Doppler (DD) channels, showing that the effective channel at a practical receiver is generally not a superposition of pure path-wise DD components. Waveform simulations verify the derived relation to machine precision, while the conventional sequence-level I/O relation for DT-AFDM exhibits a substantial mismatch with waveform behavior for practical channels with continuous-valued delays.

title: ES-Merging: Biological MLLM Merging via Embedding Space Signals
summary: Biological multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have emerged as powerful foundation models for scientific discovery. However, existing models are specialized to a single modality, limiting their ability to solve inherently cross-modal scientific problems. While model merging is an efficient method to combine the different modalities into a unified MLLM, existing methods rely on input-agnostic parameter space heuristics that fail to faithfully capture modality specialization. To overcome this limitation, we propose the Embedding-Signal-based MLLM Merging (ES-Merging), a framework that estimates merging coefficients from embedding space signals, moving the merging paradigm from the parameter signals to the embedding signals. ES-Merging exploits coarse-grained and fine-grained signals from embedding space to estimate the layer-wise and element-wise merging coefficients, respectively, which are jointly combined for complementary coefficient estimation. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that ES-Merging outperforms existing merging methods not only on the cross-modal reasoning but also on the single-modal knowledge preservation, establishing that embedding space signals provide a principled and effective foundation for MLLM merging.

title: Convex algebras on an interval with semicontinuous monotone operations
summary: In a recent work of Matteo Mio on compact quantitative equational theories (here compact means that all its consequences are derivable by means of finite proofs) convex algebras on the carrier set [0,1] whose operations are monotone and satisfy certain semicontinuity properties occurred. We fully classify those algebraic structures by giving an explicit construction of all possible convex operations on [0,1] possessing the mentioned properties. Our result thus describes exactly the range of theories to which Mio's theorem applies.

title: Edge AI and TinyML for Resource-Constrained Agriculture: Hardware Platforms, Model Optimization, and Deployment Strategies
summary: Deploying artificial intelligence at the edge is increasingly important for systems that must operate under strict limits on memory, computation, energy, connectivity, and hardware cost. Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) represents the most resource-constrained regime of this shift, enabling inference on microcontroller-class devices with tightly bounded flash and SRAM budgets. This study examines recent deployment trends in Edge AI and TinyML using precision farming as a representative real-world environment in which sensing nodes, gateways, UAVs, and embedded processors must often operate with intermittent connectivity and limited power. The analysis emphasizes the deployment stack rather than predictive accuracy alone, covering hardware classes, software toolchains, model- and system-level optimization, intelligence placement, and hardware-resource reporting. Across the analyzed studies, microcontroller-class platforms such as ESP32, STM32, and ATmega are prominent endpoint targets, while single-board computers and embedded accelerators support more compute-intensive workloads. Among the studies included in the optimization comparison, almost 50% report quantization, making reduced-precision inference the most frequently identified strategy within this subset. In contrast, structured pruning, hardware-aware neural architecture search, and coordinated cross-layer optimization remain comparatively limited. Resource profiling is also inconsistent as flash, peak RAM, MAC count, latency, and energy per inference are not reported uniformly, limiting reproducibility and comparisons across deployments. A recurring systems-level pattern is an inference-training asymmetry in which inference moves toward local devices while training and model lifecycle management remain predominantly centralized.

title: Evasive Intelligence: Lessons from Malware Analysis for Evaluating AI Agents
summary: Tool-using artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly adopted as systems that plan, observe their environment, and take actions over extended time periods. This shift challenges the current evaluation practice, in which models are tested in restricted, fully observable settings. We argue that such evaluations are vulnerable to a failure mode long known in computer security: a system that behaves benignly when it detects that it is being analyzed. Malware has exploited this for decades, by probing sandboxes, virtual machines, and instrumentation, before revealing its payload. The shared challenge is that the subject under observation can detect the conditions of its evaluation, so the setup used to observe behavior ends up shaping the behavior observed, yielding overly optimistic safety and robustness assessments. Recent AI-safety studies demonstrate pieces of this risk, though only preliminarily and under controlled conditions. Drawing on decades of malware-analysis experience, we outline concrete principles for evaluating AI agents as potentially adversarial: explicitly threat-modeling evaluator-discrimination; testing across harness variants and reporting the worst case; using shadow executions to provide a realistic runtime without irreversible side effects; treating environment probing as a risk signal; and performing unpredictable reassessments after deployment.

title: FlatLands: Indoor floormap completion from a single egocentric view
comments: 38 pages, 18 figures. Under review. Updated manuscript, title, abstract, and experiments
summary: A single egocentric image typically captures only a small portion of the floor, yet a complete metric traversability map of the surroundings would better serve applications such as indoor navigation. We introduce FlatLands, a dataset and benchmark for single-view indoor floor-map completion in metric bird's-eye view (BEV), evaluating eleven models: both deterministic and generative. FlatLands contain 270,575 observations from 17,656 scene records across six metric 3D datasets, with aligned observation, visibility, validity, and ground-truth maps and both in- and out-of-distribution protocols. We compare training-free, deterministic, ensemble, and generative methods on shared geometry-derived inputs and, without fine-tuning, on maps estimated from real egocentric RGB images. Our results show that predicting floor almost everywhere can achieve high IoU when most evaluated cells are floor, while generative sample sets outperform the best single-output model under a proper scoring rule and support safer risk-weighted planning. FlatLands establishes a rigorous testbed for evaluating both floor-map accuracy and how effectively alternative completions represent the ambiguity of unseen space.

title: Contingency-Aware Planning via Certified Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability
summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides formal safety guarantees for dynamical systems, but repeatedly solving the HJ partial differential equation in changing environments limits its use in real-time planning. This paper introduces learning-based reachability and an online safety certification that together enable real-time contingency-aware planning in unknown environments with probabilistic safety guarantees. We use Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) to approximate the HJ solution operator under varying obstacle configurations. To certify the learned reach-avoid set, we recast robust scenario optimization as multiple hypothesis testings over its sublevel sets, which yields a simultaneous guarantee across candidate levels and recovers the largest certifiable volume at the prescribed safety level. Within this certified set, the induced recovery policy is guaranteed to return the system to a safe region in finite time under any admissible disturbance. Numerical results show that the learning and certification pipeline updates reach-avoid sets at real-time rates and is demonstrated on youBot simulation.

title: To See or To Please: Uncovering Visual Sycophancy and Split Beliefs in VLMs
comments: v5: corrects the alignment test of earlier versions (v1-v4), which counted explicit refusals as Visual Sycophancy; Visual Sycophancy is 28.1% (not 75.9%) and Robust Refusal 47.8% (not 0%); see Sec. 6. 21 pages
summary: When Vision-Language Models (VLMs) answer correctly, do they rely on the image? We introduce a Tri-Layer Diagnostic Framework that asks three questions of every (image, question) pair when the image is blanked: does the model register that the image is missing (Latent Anomaly Detection, LAD), does its output distribution depend on the image (Visual Necessity Score, VNS), and does it nonetheless commit to a content answer? The cascade assigns each pair of any existing benchmark to one of four modes: Perceptual Blindness, Language Shortcut, Visual Sycophancy (the blank image registers and matters, yet the model commits to a fabricated answer), or Robust Refusal. Across nine open-weight VLMs and 9,000 model-sample pairs, 28.1% are Visual Sycophancy, 18.6% Language Shortcut, 5.6% Perceptual Blindness, and 47.8% Robust Refusal. The modes are strongly model-specific: the Qwen3-VL models refuse on blank input in 93-98% of pairs, whereas Pixtral-12B commits to an answer in 72%. Within-generation scaling increases Visual Sycophancy in both Qwen2.5-VL (7B->72B: 25.5->40.1%) and Llama-3.2-Vision (11B->90B: 34.3->48.0%), while the newer Qwen3-VL generation nearly eliminates it. A blinded human study confirms that LAD and VNS track what annotators observe, and that 80% of Visual-Sycophancy responses carry no textual sign that the image was blank.

title: EchoKV: Efficient KV Cache Compression via Similarity-Based Reconstruction
summary: The increasing memory demand of the Key-Value (KV) cache poses a significant bottleneck for Large Language Models (LLMs) in long-context applications. Existing low-rank KV compression methods reduce this footprint by modifying model projections, limiting the flexibility to switch back to standard full-cache inference when sufficient memory is available. In this paper, we propose EchoKV, a flexible KV cache compression framework that supports on-demand transitions from full KV caching to compressed caching. Unlike traditional compression-decompression paradigms, EchoKV utilizes a lightweight network to reconstruct the discarded KV components from a partial subset, exploiting intrinsic inter-layer and intra-layer similarities among attention heads. We further introduce a lightweight two-stage fine-tuning strategy, requiring only a few minutes on a single A100 GPU for Llama-3.1-8B. Experimental results on LongBench and RULER demonstrate that EchoKV offers a competitive quality-cache trade-off across multiple compression ratios and backbone models while preserving the throughput of full-cache inference in short-context scenarios.

title: Improved Algorithms for Unrelated Crowd Worker Scheduling in Mobile Social Networks
comments: 36 pages, 8 figures. v2: substantially revised. Clarified the communication model; corrected the LRF and 1.45-approximation analyses; proved that EDTS is a deterministic 1.5-approximation and added a polynomial-time (1.5+eps/2) version; redid all experiments with new baselines, optimal solutions on small instances, and running times. Submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: This paper studies task scheduling with unrelated crowd workers in mobile social networks, where the service time of a task depends on the crowd worker that performs it, and the objective is to minimize the total weighted completion time. For identical crowd workers, we tighten the approximation ratio of the Largest-Ratio-First (LRF) algorithm and update the competitive ratio of its online version. For unrelated crowd workers, we show that the time-indexed rounding framework of Im and Li remains valid when worker-dependent contact delays are added, which yields a randomized algorithm with an expected approximation ratio of 1.45; this improves upon the expected ratio of $1.5+ε$ obtained in our previous work for identical crowd workers. We also derandomize this algorithm. To improve computational efficiency, we further propose an algorithm that exploits the optimality of the Smith-ratio order on a single crowd worker, and we prove that it is a deterministic 1.5-approximation algorithm and that its polynomial-time version achieves an approximation ratio arbitrarily close to 1.5. Experiments on synthetic instances and on instances derived from real contact traces show that this algorithm outperforms three variants of LRF in all tested settings, with the largest advantage when the crowd workers are highly heterogeneous, performs on par with a local-search heuristic for unrelated machines, and is within 0.4\% of the optimum on average on small instances that can be solved exactly.

title: FatigueFormer: A Physiology-Informed Model for Upper-Limb Muscle Fatigue Assessment
summary: Surface electromyographic (sEMG) signals provide information about muscle activity and function during movement. Fatigue alters multiple properties of these signals, with patterns that vary across individuals and contraction intensities. However, physiological insights into fatigue remain underused in sEMG modeling, particularly for cross-subject recognition. We introduce FatigueFormer to recognize fatigue states defined by ratings of perceived exertion (RPE). The model incorporates physiologically motivated trend grouping into sEMG encoding by organizing descriptors into increasing- and decreasing-trend streams and combining inter-window context with within-window feature interactions. To assess fatigue-state discriminability across contraction intensities, we further present an sEMG fatigue dataset collected from 30 participants at four levels of maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) and benchmark representative machine learning and deep learning methods. We evaluate performance offline under leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) and within-subject protocols and use the SWIFTIES dataset for external validation. Results support FatigueFormer's effectiveness across the examined contraction intensities and both datasets, while indicating that fatigue-related cues vary across MVC levels. An exploratory adaptation analysis shows higher FatigueFormer scores with more labeled target-user data on complete target recordings, which include calibration samples.

title: Multi-AUV Ad-hoc Networks-Based Multi-Target Tracking Based on Scene-Adaptive Embodied Intelligence
comments: Author-accepted manuscript. Published in IEEE Wireless Communications (Early Access), 2026
summary: With the rapid advancement of underwater net-working and multi-agent coordination technologies, autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) ad-hoc networks have emerged as a pivotal framework for executing complex maritime missions, such as multi-target tracking. However, traditional data-centricarchitectures struggle to maintain operational consistency under highly dynamic topological fluctuations and severely constrained acoustic communication bandwidth. This article proposes a scene-adaptive embodied intelligence (EI) architecture for multi-AUV ad-hoc networks, which re-envisions AUVs as embodied entities by integrating perception, decision-making, and physical execution into a unified cognitive loop. To materialize the functional interaction between these layers, we define a beacon-based communication and control model that treats the communication link as a dynamic constraint-aware channel, effectively bridging the gap between high-level policy inference and decentralized physical actuation. Specifically, the proposed architecture employs a three-layer functional framework and introduces a Scene-Adaptive MARL (SA-MARL) algorithm featuring a dual-path critic mechanism. By integrating a scene critic network and a general critic network through a weight-based dynamic fusion process, SA-MARL effectively decouples specialized tracking tasks from global safety constraints, facilitating autonomous policy evolution. Evaluation results demonstrate that the proposedscheme significantly accelerates policy convergence and achieves superior tracking accuracy compared to mainstream MARL approaches, maintaining robust performance even under intense environmental interference and fluid topological shifts.

title: Exploring Student Perception on Gen AI Adoption in Higher Education: A Descriptive Study
summary: The rapid proliferation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping pedagogical practices and assessment models in higher education. While institutional and educator perspectives on GenAI integration are increasingly documented, the student perspective remains comparatively underexplored. This study examines how students perceive, use, and evaluate GenAI within their academic practices, focusing on usage patterns, perceived benefits, and expectations for institutional support. Data were collected through a questionnaire administered to 436 postgraduate Computer Science students at the University of Hertfordshire and analysed using descriptive methods. The findings reveal a Confidence-Competence Paradox: although more than 60% of students report high familiarity with tools such as ChatGPT, daily academic use remains limited and confidence in effective application is only moderate. Students primarily employ GenAI for cognitive scaffolding tasks, including concept clarification and brainstorming, rather than fully automated content generation. At the same time, respondents express concerns regarding data privacy, reliability of AI-generated information, and the potential erosion of critical thinking skills. The results also indicate strong student support for integrating AI literacy into curricula and programme Knowledge, Skills, and Behaviours (KSBs). Overall, the study suggests that universities should move beyond a policing approach to GenAI and adopt a pedagogical framework that emphasises AI literacy, ethical guidance, and equitable access to AI tools.

title: HISA: Efficient Hierarchical Indexing for Fine-Grained Sparse Attention
comments: Published as a conference paper at COLM 2026
summary: Token-level sparse attention mechanisms, exemplified by DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA), achieve fine-grained key selection by scoring every historical key for each query through a lightweight indexer, then computing attention only on the selected subset. While the downstream sparse attention itself scales favorably, the indexer must still scan the entire prefix for every query, introducing an per-layer bottleneck that grows prohibitively with context length. We propose HISA (Hierarchical Indexed Sparse Attention), a plug-and-play replacement for the indexer that rewrites the search path from a flat token scan into a two-stage hierarchical procedure: (1) a block-level coarse filtering stage that scores pooled block representations to discard irrelevant regions, followed by (2) a token-level refinement stage that applies the original indexer exclusively within the retained candidate blocks. HISA preserves the identical token-level top-sparse pattern consumed by the downstream Sparse MLA operator and requires no additional training. On kernel-level benchmarks, HISA achieves up to speedup at 64K context. On Needle-in-a-Haystack and LongBench, we directly replace the indexer in DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 with our HISA indexer, without any finetuning. HISA closely matches the original DSA in quality, while substantially outperforming block-sparse baselines.

title: JDCNet Uses Confidence Gated Privileged Modality Distillation for Cost Preserving X Ray Inference
summary: Training-only privileged-modality learning uses an expensive modality during training while keeping a single-modality deployment path. We study chest radiograph (X-ray) classification with same-patient computed tomography (CT) available only during training. JDCNet adds an auxiliary CT-teacher target, the teacher's argmax label or its softmax distribution through a Kullback--Leibler term (soft-KL), only on samples whose teacher confidence exceeds a threshold; the deployed model has the same ResNet-18 computation graph as the supervised baseline. On 510 same-patient pairs from the public BIMCV-COVID19 releases of the Valencian Region Medical ImageBank (113 COVID-19, 397 non-COVID), with patient-level five-fold cross-validation and three seeds, 15 of 16 adaptively explored JDCNet configurations improved mean balanced accuracy (BA) over the supervised baseline (average $+0.020$), but none remained significant after Holm adjustment. In a pre-registered experiment with 240 batch-matched supervised restarts on the same splits, batch size had no detectable effect on the baseline (BA $0.620$ versus $0.625$), and when both methods selected one of 16 runs per cell on the validation partition, JDCNet exceeded supervised training by $+0.037$ BA (95\% confidence interval $+0.016$ to $+0.058$; patient-level $+0.007$ to $+0.068$). Logit distillation and contrastive alignment did not help. Teacher diagnostics indicate that the gate acts mainly as CT-informed sample weighting. All models, including JDCNet, performed at chance on an external radiograph set. Confidence-gated CT supervision thus gives a small within-cohort advantage on one public cohort and a binary task; generalization requires independent paired replication.

title: On the average-case complexity landscape for Tensor-Isomorphism-complete problems over finite fields
comments: 60 pages, add average-case polynomial-time algorithm for orthogonal tensor isomorphism over finite field
summary:
In Grochow and Qiao (\emph{SIAM J. Comput.}, 2023), the complexity class Tensor Isomorphism (TI) was introduced and isomorphism problems for groups, algebras, and polynomials were shown to be TI-complete. In this paper, we study average-case algorithms for several TI-complete problems over finite fields, including algebra isomorphism, matrix code conjugacy, and $4$-tensor isomorphism.
  Our main results reveal a rich landscape of average-case complexities of Tensor Isomorphism problems, despite their equivalence in the worst-case setting. Over the finite field of order $q$, we devise (1) average-case \emph{polynomial-time} algorithms for algebra isomorphism and matrix code conjugacy that succeed for $1/Θ(q)$ fraction of inputs; (2) an average-case \emph{polynomial-time} algorithm for the $4$-tensor isomorphism that succeeds for $1/q^{Θ(1)}$ fraction of inputs; and (3) an average-case \emph{polynomial-time} algorithm for the orthogonal $3$-tensor isomorphism that succeed for $1-1/\poly(n)$ fraction of $n\times n\times n$ tensors.
  Our main technical contribution is to introduce the spectral properties of random matrices into algorithms for TI-complete problems. This leads to not only new algorithms but also new questions in random matrix theory over finite fields. To settle these questions, we need to extend both the generating function approach as in Neumann and Praeger (\emph{J. London Math. Soc.}, 1998) and the character sum method of Gorodetsky and Rodgers (\emph{Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.}, 2021).

title: Fully Scalable MPC Algorithms for Euclidean Clustering: Constant Approximation in Constant Rounds
summary:
We study Euclidean $k$-Means and $k$-Median under the Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model, focusing on the \emph{fully scalable} setting. Previously, fully scalable algorithms for $k$-Means and/or $k$-Median either required $O(\log\log n\cdot\log\log\log n)$ rounds [Cohen-Addad, Kuhn, and Parsaeian; SODA'26] or guaranteed only an $O(\log n)$-approximation [Goranci, Jiang, Kiss, Kong, Qian, and Szilagyi; SODA'26]. In this paper, we close this gap by giving the first fully scalable algorithms for both problems, which work even when $k$ is polynomially larger than the local memory, and \emph{simultaneously} achieve an $O(1)$-approximation and $O(1)$ round complexity.
  Technically, we devise a new variant of the MP algorithm [Mettu and Plaxton, SICOMP'03] that computes a \emph{fractional solution satisfying the Lagrangian Multiplier Preserving (LMP) property}. Importantly, this LMP guarantee holds even under arbitrary distance distortions, a feature that is crucial for efficient MPC implementations. We then give a novel MPC rounding algorithm that first rounds to a bicriteria solution with $k+O(n^{1-ε})$ centers and then uses an \emph{iterative kernelization} idea to convert it into one with exactly $k$ centers.

title: Query-Conditioned Evidential Keyframe Sampling for MLLM-Based Long-Form Video Understanding
summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown strong performance on video question answering, but their application to long-form videos is constrained by limited context length and computational cost, making keyframe sampling essential. Existing approaches typically rely on semantic relevance or reinforcement learning, which either fail to capture evidential clues or suffer from inefficient combinatorial optimization. In this work, we propose an evidence-driven keyframe sampling framework motivated by an information-theoretic perspective. We consider maximizing the conditional mutual information between the selected frames and the answer given the query as an idealized objective, and use a modular singleton-gain surrogate to motivate a tractable frame-wise selection criterion. Guided by this motivation, we train a query-conditioned evidence scoring network using annotated answer-supporting segments. A contrastive objective encourages greater aggregate score mass on frames from evidence regions than on background frames, providing a practical evidence-based criterion beyond semantic similarity. Experiments on long-form video understanding benchmarks show that our method consistently outperforms prior sampling strategies under comparable frame budgets. With Qwen2.5-VL-7B under the same 32-frame budget, our method improves over uniform sampling by 10.1 points on LVBench and 4.4 points on the long-video subset of VideoMME.

title: UQ-SHRED: uncertainty quantification of shallow recurrent decoder networks for sparse sensing via engression
summary: Reconstructing high-dimensional spatiotemporal fields from sparse sensor measurements is critical in a wide range of scientific applications. The SHallow REcurrent Decoder (SHRED) architecture is a recent state-of-the-art architecture that reconstructs high-quality spatial domain from hyper-sparse sensor measurement streams. An important limitation of SHRED is that in complex, data-scarce, high-frequency, or stochastic systems, portions of the spatiotemporal field must be modeled with valid uncertainty estimation. We introduce UQ-SHRED, a distributional learning framework for sparse sensing problems that provides uncertainty quantification through a neural network-based distributional regression called engression. UQ-SHRED models the uncertainty by learning the predictive distribution of the spatial state conditioned on the sensor history. By injecting stochastic noise into sensor inputs and training with an energy score loss, UQ-SHRED produces predictive distributions with minimal computational overhead, requiring only noise injection at the input and resampling through a single architecture without retraining or additional network structures. On complicated synthetic and real-life datasets including turbulent flow, atmospheric dynamics, neuroscience and astrophysics, UQ-SHRED provides a distributional approximation with well-calibrated confidence intervals. We further conduct ablation studies to understand how each model setting affects the quality of the UQ-SHRED performance, and its validity on uncertainty quantification over a set of different experimental setups.

title: VideoZeroBench: Probing the Limits of Video MLLMs with Spatio-Temporal Evidence Verification
summary: Video multimodal large language models achieve strong results on existing benchmarks, but answer accuracy alone does not establish whether they can locate the evidence needed to answer a question. We introduce VideoZeroBench, a challenging long-video benchmark with manually annotated question-answer pairs spanning 13 video domains. Questions target fine-grained cues, fleeting events, and evidence distributed across multiple segments. Temporal intervals and key-frame boxes are annotated where applicable. All questions undergo two rounds of cross-verification for answer validity and evidence quality. Our five-level diagnostic protocol compares answering with and without evidence hints, then combines answer correctness with independently evaluated temporal and spatial grounding. Across 19 evaluated models, the best standard QA accuracy is 24.8% (Level-3), achieved by Gemini-3.7-Flash. No model exceeds 1.8% when correct answers and accurate spatio-temporal localization are jointly required (Level-5). Analyses of atomic abilities, evidence spans, input modalities, and thinking-with-videos inference further characterize where the evaluated systems struggle. These findings motivate more precise evidence search and localization for long-video question answering. Our code and data are publicly released.

title: Compositional Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
summary: We study structured abstraction-based reasoning for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) and compare its generalization to test-time approaches. Purely neural architectures lack reliable combinatorial generalization, while strictly symbolic systems struggle with perceptual grounding. We therefore propose a neuro-symbolic architecture that extracts object-level structure from grids, uses neural priors to propose candidate transformations from a fixed domain-specific language (DSL) of atomic patterns, and filters hypotheses using cross-example consistency checks. Instantiated as a compositional reasoning framework based on unit patterns inspired by human visual abstraction, the system augments large language models (LLMs) with object representations and transformation proposals. On ARC-AGI-2, it improves over the base solver LLM (Grok-4, 16.0%) to 24.4% on the public evaluation set, and to 30.8% when combined with ARC Lang Solver via a meta-classifier. These results support the claim that in the evaluated settings, allocating test-time compute to object abstraction, neural-guided transformation proposal, and consistency filtering can improve accuracy over unstructured sampling-based scaling without task-specific finetuning of the system. We open-source the code: (https://github.com/CoreThink-AI/arc-agi-2-reasoner).

title: Adaptive Local Frequency Filtering for Fourier-Encoded Implicit Neural Representations
summary: Implicit neural representations (INRs) commonly employ Fourier features to alleviate spectral bias and represent high-frequency signals. Fourier encodings, however, use the same frequency representation across spatial locations despite the spatially varying frequency content of natural signals. We propose Adaptive Frequency Implicit Neural Representation (AFINR), a spatially adaptive frequency-conditioning framework for Fourier encoded INRs. A sampling compatible Fourier dictionary first defines the explicit frequency support, and a learnable spatial control field then modulates the admitted Fourier components before decoding. The control field is parameterized in the discrete cosine transform (DCT) domain to provide a compact and continuously queryable spatial representation. AFINR can be combined with different coordinate decoders, including ReLU, SIREN, CAFE, and CAFE+. Experiments on Kodak and DIV2K show consistent average improvements across these decoder families. In particular, AFINR-CAFE+ improves CAFE+ by 3.95 dB on Kodak and 3.50 dB on DIV2K. Ablation studies characterize the effects of adaptive-field parameterization, DCT coefficient retention, and frequency-response parameters, while learned spatial responses show position-dependent use of the admitted Fourier components.

title: Low-Degree Learning from Localization Schemes
comments: 57 pages This paper subsumes an earlier version of this work by the same authors
summary:
The low-degree algorithm is a cornerstone in computational learning theory. For product or Gaussian distributions, it shows that efficiently learnability follows from Fourier concentration. However, a longstanding obstacle towards building such a theory over nonproduct distributions is that we can no longer rely on having closed-form expressions for a good basis of orthogonal functions. This hints that the analysis of the low-degree algorithm might be brittle to the underlying distributional assumptions.
  We refute this intuition by showing that the low-degree algorithm provably succeeds for a large class of graphical models under mild high-temperature conditions. As an application, for nearly every Ising model that is known to rapidly mix, we obtain learning algorithms for every function class for which the Fourier approach succeeds for product distributions (e.g. low-depth circuits, halfspaces, intersections, monotone, among others) with no significant loss. Our framework is based on a strikingly clean connection with the coordinate-by-coordinate localization scheme of Chen and Eldan introduced for establishing rapid mixing in high-temperature models, as well as other analytical transference principles to product distributions.

summary: LoRA enables efficient customization of LLMs and is widely used in multi-tenant and multi-task serving. title: How Does Machine Learning Manage Complexity?
summary:
We provide a computational complexity lens to understand the power of machine learning models, particularly their ability to model complex systems.
  Machine learning models are often trained on data drawn from sampleable or more complex distributions, a far wider range of distributions than just computable ones. By focusing on computable distributions, machine learning models can better manage complexity via probability. We abstract away from specific learning mechanisms, modeling machine learning as producing P/poly-computable distributions with polynomially-bounded max-entropy.
  We illustrate how learning computable distributions models complexity by showing that if a machine learning model produces a distribution $μ$ that models the distribution generated by a cryptographic pseudorandom generator at least as well as the uniform distribution does, then $μ$ must be close to uniform.
  We view training as compression that removes the randomness from the data, keeping only its structure, and inference as adding randomness back to generate new outputs. A computationally bounded model cannot distinguish pseudorandomness from true randomness, so training removes both, treating anything it cannot efficiently predict as noise. The same holds at inference, where the randomness added back can be, and in practice is, pseudorandom.
  In the appendix, we make the connection to compression precise and, using a characterization of pseudoentropy by Vadhan and Zheng, show that the best loss achievable by an efficient model is the next-bit pseudoentropy of the data.

title: TorchUMM: A Unified Multimodal Model Codebase for Evaluation, Analysis, and Post-training
summary: Recent advances in unified multimodal models (UMMs) have led to a proliferation of architectures capable of understanding, generating, and editing across visual and textual modalities. However, developing a unified framework for UMMs remains challenging due to the diversity of model architectures and the heterogeneity of training paradigms and implementation details. In this paper, we present TorchUMM, the first unified codebase for comprehensive evaluation, analysis, and post-training across diverse UMM backbones, tasks, and datasets. TorchUMM supports a broad spectrum of models covering a wide range of scales and design paradigms. Our benchmark encompasses three core task dimensions: multimodal understanding, generation, and editing, and integrates both established and novel datasets to evaluate perception, reasoning, compositionality, and instruction-following abilities. By providing a unified interface and standardized evaluation protocols, TorchUMM enables fair and reproducible comparisons across heterogeneous models and fosters deeper insights into their strengths and limitations, facilitating the development of more capable unified multimodal systems. title: Block Diagram Analysis of an Amplitude-Frequency Design Principle in Biological Oscillators
summary: An important design principle for biological oscillators divides oscillators into two types: fixed frequency, variable amplitude and fixed amplitude, variable frequency. Because of the interplay of nonlinearity and feedback, both positive and negative, analytical investigations of this design principle are primarily based on numerical simulations of ordinary differential equations. To enhance the qualitative and quantitative characterization of this design principle, we adapted and developed a block diagram modeling framework. We showed how the observed amplitude-frequency characteristics could be obtained from the block diagram models of both the types of oscillators. We obtained explicit constraints on the positive feedback and negative feedback strengths for the oscillations to exist. We represented both types of oscillators in a single unifying, control-theoretic framework that connects both the types of oscillators under a single theoretical model. These results contribute to a systems and control perspective on oscillations in biology and related contexts.

title: Scalable Exact Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering via Sparse Geographic Distance Graphs
summary: Exact hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC) of large spatial datasets is limited in practice by the $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ time and memory required for the full pairwise distance matrix. We present GSHAC (Geographically Sparse Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering), a system that makes exact HAC feasible at scales of millions of geographic features on a commodity workstation. GSHAC replaces the distance matrix with a sparse geographic distance graph containing only pairs within a user-specified geodesic bound $h_{\max}$, constructed in $\mathcal{O}(n \cdot k)$ time via spatial indexing, where $k$ is the mean number of neighbors within $h_{\max}$. Connected components of this graph define independent subproblems, and we prove that the resulting assignments are exact for all standard linkage methods at any cut height $h \le h_{\max}$. For single linkage, an MST-based path keeps memory at $\mathcal{O}(n_k + m_k)$ per component. Applied to a global mining inventory ($n = 261{,}073$), the system completes in 12 s (109 MiB peak HAC memory) versus $\approx 545$ GiB for the dense baseline. On a 2-million-point GeoNames sample, all tested thresholds completed in under 3 minutes with peak memory under 3 GiB. We provide a scikit-learn-compatible implementation for direct integration into GIS workflows.

title: Latent-Condensed Transformer for Efficient Long Context Modeling
summary: Large language models (LLMs) face significant challenges in processing long contexts due to the linear growth of the key-value (KV) cache and quadratic complexity of self-attention. Existing approaches address these bottlenecks separately: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) reduces the KV cache by projecting tokens into a low-dimensional latent space, while sparse attention reduces computation. However, sparse methods cannot operate natively on MLA's compressed latent structure, missing opportunities for joint optimization. In this paper, we propose Latent-Condensed Attention (LCA), which directly condenses context within MLA's latent space, where the representation is disentangled into semantic latent vectors and positional keys. LCA separately aggregates semantic vectors via query-aware pooling and preserves positional keys via anchor selection. This approach jointly reduces both computational cost and KV cache without adding parameters. Beyond MLA, LCA's design is architecture-agnostic and readily extends to other attention mechanisms such as GQA. Theoretically, we prove a length-independent error bound. Experiments show LCA achieves up to 2.5$\times$ prefilling speedup and 90% KV cache reduction at 128K context while maintaining competitive performance.

title: Capability-Aware Heterogeneous Control Barrier Functions for Decentralized Multi-Robot Safe Navigation
summary: Safe decentralized navigation in heterogeneous robot teams is challenging because robots with different dynamics and control limits cannot satisfy identical collision-avoidance obligations equally well. Existing methods often rely on model-specific safety formulations or allocate avoidance responsibility without considering whether the assigned control is physically realizable, possibly leading to safety-constrained QP infeasibility and safety violations. We propose Capability-Aware Heterogeneous Control Barrier Functions (CA-HCBF), a decentralized framework for consistent safety enforcement and capability-aware responsibility allocation. We derive a unified operational-space second-order control-affine formulation for holonomic and nonholonomic mobile robots through canonical transformation and backstepping, addressing the relative-degree mismatch while preserving forward invariance of the pairwise safe set. Second, we quantify each robot's achievable control authority along the safety-critical direction using a support-function-based capability metric and use it to distribute pairwise avoidance responsibility. A feasibility-aware clipping mechanism further mitigates physically unrealizable responsibility assignments. Simulations with up to 30 heterogeneous robots and hardware experiments demonstrate high task completion with low safety violations and reduction in local QP infeasibility.
