title: HTAM: Hierarchical Transition-Attended Memory for Operator Optimization
summary: High-performance GPU kernels are essential for efficient LLM deployment, yet optimizing them remains expertise-intensive. Recent LLM-based code generation makes automatic GPU operator generation promising, but operator optimization remains a hardware-aware search problem. Existing LLM-based methods face a granularity mismatch: coarse hints are reusable but hard to execute, whereas detailed memories are actionable but enlarge the search space and obscure optimization bottlenecks. The key challenge is therefore to organize optimization experience at an appropriate granularity. To address this issue, this paper proposes HTAM (Hierarchical Transition-Attended Memory), a coarse-to-fine framework for LLM-based operator optimization. HTAM builds a two-level Hierarchical Transition Graph (HTG) to organize coarse global directions, detailed local strategies, and transition experience between optimization steps. During each evolution step, HTAM selects a global direction from the current state and recent optimization history, retrieves the corresponding local strategy memory, and uses it to guide concrete CUDA code generation. Experiments on KernelBench demonstrate that HTAM improves correctness, fast-solution rate, and speedup over LLM-based baselines, while backend and Robust-KBench studies indicate transferable benefits from structured memory.

title: DynaFLIP: Rethinking Robotics Perception via Tri-Modal-Dynamics Guided Representation
summary: Robot manipulation critically depends on perception that preserves the action-relevant aspects of a scene. Yet most robot learning pipelines are built upon visual encoders pre-trained for static recognition or vision-language alignment, leaving motion understanding to downstream policies. We introduce DynaFLIP, a dynamics-aware multimodal pre-training framework that pushes motion understanding upstream into perception. We construct image-language-3D flow triplets from heterogeneous human and robot videos, and use these triplets as training-time supervision to shape an image-only encoder. Our key idea is to encourage the three modalities to span a small simplex volume in the shared hyperspherical space -- a smaller simplex volume indicating stronger alignment. To avoid the geometric ambiguity and trivial collapse of naive volume minimization, we combine simplex-volume minimization with a cosine regularizer and a contrastive objective. Our analyses show that DynaFLIP focuses on control-relevant regions critical for manipulation. The resulting dynamics-aware representations serve as reusable visual backbones and consistently outperform baselines across diverse downstream policies, including VLAs. We validate this across diverse simulation and real-world setups, with gains reaching +22.5% under out-of-distribution scenarios. Our results suggest that robot generalization improves when visual representations are trained to encode not just what is present, but how the world changes under action.

title: SlotMemory: Object-Centric KV Memory for Streaming Long-Video Generation
summary: Streaming video generation models typically rely on temporal-centric memory, organizing historical context as latent queues, compressed context tokens, or unclustered token sets. This often causes identity drift and semantic inconsistency when entities exit the frame or during interactive prompt transitions. To address these limitations, we propose SlotMemory, an object-centric Key-Value (KV) memory mechanism for streaming video diffusion. Our approach shifts memory abstraction from ``when'' an event occurred to ``what'' is represented by decomposing the transformer's KV manifold into discrete, reusable semantic slots. Because the slots serve only as routing addresses and the stored content remains the original transformer KV tokens, the mechanism adds entity-level persistence and prompt-aware retrieval across long horizons. Evaluated on 60-second interactive narratives using the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B backbone, SlotMemory achieves the highest Dynamic Degree among evaluated streaming methods and the second-highest aggregate Quality Score, preserving prompt adherence rather than trading it away for consistency. At the 30-second horizon, SlotMemory leads in Total, Quality, and Dynamic Degree, improving Dynamic Degree by 31.2% over MemFlow, the strongest memory-based baseline. Our results support treating structured semantic representation, rather than raw temporal capacity, as a critical primitive for persistent long-form video synthesis.

title: Toward Identifiable Sparse Autoencoders
comments: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) 2026. This version corrects the proof of Theorem 3.6; see Appendix
summary: Recently, sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have emerged as an attractive tool for interpreting and interacting with representations in practical neural networks. While it is common empirical folklore, we also show theoretically that SAEs are highly unstable: different training runs are likely to produce different concept dictionaries and sparse codes. We characterize the model properties that hinder the stability of real-world SAEs, and address each of these problems through minimal changes to the architecture and training procedure. Together, these changes yield two versions of an \textbf{i}dentifiable SAE (iSAE), a variant of the standard TopK SAE with lower reconstruction error and improved stability. We explain this improvement theoretically by connecting SAEs with traditional dictionary learning approaches, and show that the dictionaries learned in practice satisfy an approximate restricted isometry condition, rendering the corresponding sparse codes in those models near-identifiable.

title: Personalized to Persuade: The Effects of Contextualization and Warmth on Trust and Reliance in Conversational AI
summary: Contextualization is a form of personalization in which the message is framed in a context meaningful to the recipient, using their interests and background. Personalization is a known persuasive strategy of artificial intelligence (AI) systems in politics and marketing. However, the persuasive effect of contextualization in everyday tasks, where users often lack prior knowledge, remains unclear. We ran a $2\times2$ between-subjects experiment ($N = 407$) in a fictional scenario where participants had no prior opinions or knowledge. We examined how contextualization, combined with conversational warmth, shapes the persuasive power of an AI assistant arguing against expert recommendations and users' reliance on it. Our findings show that the neutral, non-contextualized assistant was the most persuasive. Contextualization and warmth each reduced persuasiveness on their own, but their interaction increased it. Reliance was present in all conditions, and neither cue changed it detectably. Trust predicted persuasion and reliance, yet neither contextualization nor warmth had an indirect effect through trust. Participants with higher self-reported AI literacy relied more on the assistant without trusting it more. Our study extends AI personalization research from political opinions to everyday decisions made without prior knowledge. The results suggest that users are more likely to be persuaded by, and defer to, an AI assistant than an expert, even without personalization. AI persuasion experiments should therefore include untailored assistants and measure decisions; the cues that changed persuasion did not detectably change reliance.

title: Beyond Augmentation: Score-Guided Pathological Prior for EEG-based Depression Detection
comments: Revised version with corrected experimental configurations and baseline evaluation protocols
summary:
Deep learning-based Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) detection using Electroencephalography (EEG) is fundamentally constrained by the "small-sample dilemma." Prevailing generative data augmentation methods not only incur heavy computational overhead but also risk introducing synthetic noise, thereby blurring classification boundaries. To challenge the traditional "data quantity first" convention, we propose a novel framework "Beyond Augmentation": Score-Guided Classification (SGC). SGC does not synthesize pseudo-samples; instead, it utilizes an unsupervised generative network architecture to model the structural and statistical anomaly degrees of samples, serving as the core "Pathological Prior". This prior, after robust normalization, is explicitly fused with deep feature representations, thereby precisely guiding the classifier's decision boundary. Furthermore, to dynamically adapt to varying channel configurations, we propose a Cross-Channel Spatial Adaptation module, utilizing a spatial mapping mechanism to effectively resolve the hardware heterogeneity of mismatched channels in multi-center datasets. Extensive experiments on the Mumtaz2016 and high-density MODMA datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and exceptional generalizability of our method under the challenging "zero data augmentation" setting and at "zero sample synthesis cost".

title: αDepth: Learning Scene-Level Soft Boundary Decomposition for Stereo Conversion
summary: Accurately modeling soft boundaries, e.g., hair and defocus blur, is a fundamental challenge in stereo conversion due to the ambiguous blending of foreground and background. Existing depth models primarily predict single-layer depth, leading to ambiguity in depth correspondence at soft boundaries. While matting techniques can capture opacity for layered modeling, they often struggle in complex scenes with multiple targets and usually require user intervention. This paper introduces αDepth, a layered representation that decomposes soft boundaries for high-fidelity stereo conversion. Specifically, we first resolve mixed color and depth ambiguity by estimating layered color and depth values at soft boundaries. Considering complex multi-target scenes, we design a Circular Alpha Representation (CAR) that shifts the paradigm from global target extraction to local boundary decomposition. Unlike prior matting methods restricted to a single foreground/background, CAR enables efficient scene-level inference without manual guidance. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that αDepth achieves state-of-the-art performance in stereo conversion, eliminating background bleeding and structural distortions at soft boundaries.

title: Generate in Reconstruction Space, Match in Semantic Space: Transport Geometry for One-Step Generation
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 26 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. Code: https://github.com/Genentech/semantic-transport-generation
summary: Generative modeling and self-supervised representation learning (SSL) optimize structurally different objectives: generative training rewards distributional fidelity, while SSL rewards semantic coherence. Yet recent work repeatedly finds that SSL features improve generative training, though the mechanism of this synergy remains unclear. Here, we study the benefits of SSL in generative modeling in the framework of one-step generation where the role of representation is explicit: frozen SSL features are used to match generated samples to real data. We use the Sinkhorn divergence in that feature space, providing a tractable surrogate for the Wasserstein distance, the population-level discrepancy approximated by Fréchet-style evaluation metrics (such as FID). We find that this objective becomes highly effective when computed in a semantically structured SSL feature space (a 39$\times$ reduction in ImageNet FID). We trace this behavior primarily to matching estimation: semantic SSL features that suppress nuisance reconstruction details induce a more compact geometry, making distribution matching more tractable. As a consequence, the best training SSL features need not match the features used by the evaluation metric. In particular, we show that using Inception as the feature extractor can improve FID while degrading matching stability and sample quality, revealing a form of metric hacking. Using extensive experiments on ImageNet, we identify which SSL feature families lead to best generation performance and show that matching stability is a quantitative criterion for selecting them. Code is available at https://github.com/Genentech/semantic-transport-generation.

title: PACE: Phase-Aware Chunk Execution for Robot Policies with Action Chunking
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 33 pages including appendices and the paper checklist. Updated experiments, discussion, references, and author list
summary: Action-chunking robot policies predict sequences of future actions, but deployment requires choosing how many actions to execute before replanning. The execution horizon trades off feedback frequency against motion continuity. However, success varies non-monotonically with the execution horizon, and the best-performing horizon differs across tasks. These effects make a single fixed horizon unreliable as a default execution strategy across tasks. We propose PACE (Phase-Aware Chunk Execution), a training-free method that selects execution horizons online from predicted action chunks. PACE uses prominent low-speed valleys in the predicted speed profile as candidate replanning boundaries, exploiting the phase-dependent kinematics of manipulation trajectories. By default, PACE calibrates the valley threshold from each task's existing training demonstrations, without task-specific fixed-horizon tuning. On the 50-task RoboTwin2.0 benchmark, PACE improves average success from 57.8% to 64.2% over the strongest fixed-horizon baseline and outperforms the adaptive execution baselines AAC and AutoHorizon. With GR00T N1.7 on LIBERO, PACE achieves the highest overall success rate among the evaluated strategies, supporting its applicability across base policies, benchmarks, and action representations. On real robots, PACE improves the average task score from 60.7 to 77.7 and success rate from 50.7% to 70.4% over full-chunk execution. Code is available at https://niejunnan25.github.io/pace-project/.

title: Domination-Avoiding Learning Agents Cannot Collude
comments: 27 pages, 1 figure. Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 (Spotlight). Camera-ready version
summary: An influential paper of Calvano et al. empirically demonstrated that Q-learning agents spontaneously collude when placed as sellers that compete on prices in a natural market model. More recent results of Fish et al. empirically demonstrated that similar collusion happens with commercial LLMs. We formally prove that such collusion can also happen with external-regret-minimizing agents. We identify a very general class of agents, which we term Domination-Avoiding agents, that provably do not collude in such markets. This class contains all Mean-Based agents and all internal-regret-minimizing agents, as well as others such as Multiplicative-Weight agents with variable learning rate and contextual variants thereof. More generally we show that, in any game, this class of agents is guaranteed to jointly learn to almost never play strategies that are eliminated by repeated elimination of purely dominated strategies.

title: Conditional Collapse in Sign Language Production: A Diagnostic and a Coverage Argument
comments: 23 pages. v2: adds Phoenix-2014T, CSL-Daily and ASL3DWord experiments, the conditioning-coverage analysis, and a frame-level DTW analysis; appendix included
summary: The goal of Sign Language Production (SLP) is to translate natural language text into corresponding sign language movements performed by a virtual avatar. The quality of the generated motion is typically evaluated by a motion-space Frechet distance (FID) and back-translation BLEU score on benchmarks such as How2Sign. The existing approaches can improve both metrics substantially while the underlying generator fails to represent the input sentence, a failure we call conditional collapse. In this work we propose to evaluate the generated motion at three independent levels: (tau1) initial-pose conditioning, (tau2) output diversity, and (tau3) target faithfulness. We compute these as pairwise-distance ratios using latent representations of a frozen motion autoencoder (MoAE), judged against each dataset's own GT-vs-GT reference. We evaluate diffusion and regression SLP models on How2Sign, including a re-implemented Neural Sign Actors, and show that tau3 faithfulness is never attained, while FID varies by nearly two orders of magnitude and is uncorrelated with faithfulness. We then apply the same models and diagnostic to Phoenix-2014T, CSL-Daily, and gloss-level ASL3DWord and show that faithfulness varies proportionally to how densely the training sentences cover the test conditions (conditioning coverage) and not corpus size. The smaller but densely covered Phoenix-2014T and ASL3DWord datasets generate faithful sign motion, while CSL-Daily follows the input text yet falls short of sign language faithfulness. Using the largest, open-domain How2Sign dataset, the models collapse at every scale. We introduce two measurements of the text data that rank the corpora in the order of how densely the training sentences fill the embedding space, and how close each test sentence lies to its nearest training sentence.

title: Coherent Off-Policy Improvement of Large Behavior Models with Learned Rewards
summary: Distilling expert demonstration data into large generative models using behavioral cloning is a scalable approach to learning capable policies for robotic control, particularly for dexterous manipulation. Reinforcement learning (RL) can be used as a means to finetune these policies further using additional experience. An open question is whether RL is more sample-efficient than collecting more expert demonstrations. Prior work has finetuned large pretrained policies in a scalable fashion by applying RL to a smaller residual policy that corrects the pretrained model. However, for typical sparse reward tasks, RL algorithms can struggle to optimize the behavior in a sample-efficient manner. We explore inverse reinforcement learning, where a dense reward function is learned from expert demonstrations, potentially reducing the challenge of RL finetuning. We specifically consider coherent imitation learning, an IRL method that facilitates improvement of the BC policy by using a specific learned reward formulation with theoretical guarantees for imitation learning. We show that our IRL method maintains or improves the performance of pi-0.5 on all six sparse manipulation tasks and achieves a $\geq 90\%$ success rate on five out of six complex manipulation tasks, outperforming RL-based baselines using sparse rewards. We also demonstrate real-world learning on a robot manipulation task, finetuning pi-0.5 to success with less than 30 minutes of environment interaction time. By ensuring our initial pretrained finetuning policy is optimal for our initial reward and critic, our method circumvents the initial drop commonly seen in RL finetuning and enables faster improvement.

title: The Price of Partial Information with Switching Costs: A Complete Characterization for Feedback Graphs
comments: 70 pages. Substantially expanded version: extends the two-action apple-tasting result to a complete characterization for all feedback graphs. Title and author list updated. Accompanying Lean formalization covers the mathematical results, excluding computational complexity claims
summary: We study how switching costs affect minimax regret under partial feedback. Which features of the feedback preserve the $\sqrt T$ rate, and which force the $T^{2/3}$ rate? We address this question in the framework of feedback graphs, which interpolate between full information and bandits: playing an action reveals the losses of its out-neighbors in a known directed graph. Prior work on feedback graphs with switching costs gave algorithms with regret of order $T^{2/3}$, but matching lower bounds only for restricted classes of graphs, leaving the question open. We establish a complete characterization of the minimax regret with switching costs for all feedback graphs: $\widetildeΘ(\sqrt T)$ if the graph is strongly revealing, meaning that every pair of distinct actions has an endpoint that observes the losses of both; $\widetildeΘ(γ^{1/3}T^{2/3})$ for every other observable graph, where $γ$ is the domination number; and linear otherwise. In particular, tournaments, in which every action observes its own loss and each pair of actions is joined by one directed edge, sit at the phase transition: they behave like full information, but deleting the edge of any pair forces the rate $T^{2/3}$. Hence an action that observes all losses is neither necessary nor sufficient for the rate $\sqrt T$. Our algorithm TournamentSteering for the strongly revealing case rests on a new principle: each observed comparison of two actions serves both to estimate losses and to steer play, and the loss reduction from steering pays for the variance of the estimates. For every strongly revealing graph, distributing the comparisons among observing actions keeps this variance, and hence the regret, polylogarithmic in the number of actions, by an argument similar to the greedy construction of logarithmic dominating sets in tournaments.

title: An Open Book, On Whose Terms? Power Dynamics in Sensor-Derived, LLM-Generated Summaries Sharing Between Older Adults and Remote Families
summary: As older adults (OAs) increasingly favor aging in place, remote family members (RFMs) need meaningful awareness of their loved ones without intrusive monitoring. Large language models can provide rich interpretations of non-intrusive sensing data, yet recent work has largely emphasized technical accuracy over how families use or benefit from this information. We conducted formative interviews with 12 RFMs and 2 OAs, followed by a three-month deployment case study with one OA-RFM dyad. Our system provided daily AI-generated summaries of multimodal sensing data, which we iteratively refined with both parties using a research-through-design approach. Although the summaries integrated well into the dyad's daily routine, sustaining over 90% engagement, their lived experience revealed evolving tensions around agency, reassurance, privacy, trust, and communication, shaped by sensor limitations and existing communication misalignments. Our findings inform the design of future AI-mediated sharing systems that account for real-world sensing constraints and complex family care dynamics.

title: SimuScene: Simulation-Ready Compositional 3D Scene Reconstruction from a Single Image
summary: Reconstructing interactive, simulation-ready 3D scenes from a single image is a critical bottleneck for robotic manipulation. While recent single-image lifters recover plausible per-object shapes, composing them yields scenes that collapse under physical simulation due to interpenetrating, hovering, or sinking objects. Existing physics-aware compositional reconstruction methods mainly address this as a post-hoc layout correction, leaving the underlying geometric errors unresolved. To address this, we introduce SimuScene, a compositional 3D reconstruction pipeline that puts physics in the loop of shape and layout estimation. Rather than using physics merely for layout cleanup, we utilize the physics engine as a diagnostic measurement tool during the generative process itself. By diagnostically simulating reconstructed objects under gravity, we convert penetration and support failures into quantitative correction signals that drive amodal shape resampling, with gravity-axis stretching as a lightweight correction for minor errors. This physics-informed feedback loop mitigates accumulated reconstruction errors and produces a stable, simulation-ready compositional 3D scene. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on physical stability and geometric alignment benchmarks. We further highlight SimuScene's utility by deploying reconstructed environments in humanoid control and robot-arm manipulation tasks.

title: LLMCodec: Adapting Video Codecs for Efficient Weight Compression of Large Language Models
summary: The rapid development of large language models(LLMs) has led to remarkable advances in natural language processing. However, the increasing scale of these models introduces substantial challenges in terms of storage, transmission, and deployment. Though great efforts have been devoted to model compression and quantization, existing methods often rely on fine-tuning or calibration data, which exhibit limited generalization across different tensor types. In this paper, we argue that video codecs offer a promising solution for LLM compression, due to their inherent compatibility with matrix structured data, configurable compression strategies, and the availability of highly optimized, off-the-shelf implementations. Therefore, we present LLMCodec, a video codec-based LLM compression method that integrates affine quantization with the recent VVC/H.266 video codec. Beyond VVC, we further compare a range of video codecs and encoding profiles to evaluate their impact on compression performance. Experiments on different models demonstrate the robustness and generality of LLMCodec. Notably, on LLaMA-3-8B at 2-bit precision, LLMCodec reduces perplexity by over 1.5x and improves downstream task accuracy by 21% compared with the existing method.

title: Settling the Complexity of Hylland--Zeckhauser Equilibria
summary: The Hylland--Zeckhauser (HZ) mechanism is a foundational framework for allocating indivisible goods in one-sided matching markets via lotteries supported by competitive prices and equal artificial budgets. We resolve the exact computational complexity of the HZ scheme by proving that computing an exact HZ equilibrium is FIXP-complete, thereby settling a conjecture of Vazirani and Yannakakis. Notably, this hardness persists even when computing the equilibrium allocation alone. We establish our hardness result via a reduction that encodes quadratic fixed-point equations into a reciprocal variational inequality. On the algorithmic side, we present a deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithm that achieves an additive error of $0.0755211 + δ$ for any $δ> 0$, significantly improving upon the previous $1/e$ guarantee.

title: IntentNav: Learning Spatial-Visual Object Navigation from Human Demonstrations
summary: Object navigation requires a robot to search for an unobserved target in an unknown environment by deciding where to explore next under partial observability. Effective search resembles human-like exploration: selectively probing visually promising frontiers while relying on spatial memory to avoid redundant revisits. We propose IntentNav, a spatial-visual imitation framework that learns human-like ObjectNav policies from human demonstrations. To infer high-level search intent from low-level human actions, we introduce Frontier-based Human-Intent Labeling, which looks ahead in human demonstrations and labels the frontier that best explains the demonstrator's future search direction. We construct a spatial-visual candidate space, where BEV memory tracks explored regions, unexplored frontiers, and trajectory history, while egocentric visual memory provides semantic cues for each candidate. A VLM policy is trained to select among these grounded candidates, using Intent-Aligned Objective to encourage consistent and human-like exploration. IntentNav achieves state-of-the-art performance among learning-based methods on the MP3D, HM3D-v1, and HM3D-v2 ObjectNav benchmarks, attaining the best success rate among all compared methods. The proposed candidate-level navigation interface transfers zero-shot to wheeled, quadruped, and humanoid robots without further VLM fine-tuning. \href{https://wmn7.github.io/IntentNav/}{Project page}.

title: How Deep Are Deep GPs, Really? A Sharp Threshold and a Non-Gaussian Limit for Compositional GPs
summary:
Compositional priors describe the generic properties of layered functions in deep Bayesian models, where deep neural networks with random weights are a canonical example. In the wide-network limit, the prior is a Gaussian process (GP) with a depth-dependent kernel, and its behaviour as depth grows has been extensively studied through this kernel. Here, we study another case, where each layer itself is a vector valued Gaussian process, and our aim is similarly to understand the limiting behaviour of the prior as depth grows.
  Previous GP work has established that for the radial basis function (RBF) kernel and a certain range of bandwidths $r$, the prior degenerates in the limit, converging to the set of constant functions, which is not useful as a probabilistic model. In this paper we establish several new results. First, we identify a sharp bandwidth threshold $r_c(d) = Θ(\sqrt{d})$ above which the limit is degenerate, strengthening the earlier bounds. Second, and more importantly, we show that for $r$ below the threshold $r_c(d)$ the prior converges to a limit distribution $π_{\bar{Z}}$. We also prove that these distributions are non-degenerate and non-Gaussian, with non-vanishing dependence between coordinates. In contrast to the previously known degenerate regime, deep Gaussian process priors can therefore admit non-trivial limits.
  Empirically, we verify the threshold across a range of dimensions $d$, and demonstrate a complex multimodal behaviour of the limit distributions $π_{\bar{Z}}$, a regime that becomes increasingly narrow with $d$ and would be hard to identify without knowing the threshold.

title: From Senses to Decisions: The Information Flow of Auditory and Visual Perception in Multimodal LLMs
summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can listen and see, but how do audio and visual signals actually travel through the network to shape an answer? Despite their growing role in research and real-world applications, the internal pathways through which audio and visual tokens influence the final prediction remain poorly understood. In this study, we examine audio-visual information flow inside Audio-Visual Large Language Models (AVLLMs), tracing how AVLLMs route, utilize, and integrate audio and visual information across two input configurations, audio-visual video and multiple interleaved audio-visual items. We find that for audio-visual video, AVLLMs follow the sequential information flow pathway established for VLMs and VideoLLMs, with audio and visual contribution flowing along this pathway in proportion to the task's reliance on each modality. In settings with multiple interleaved audio-visual items, this routing shifts to different parallel streams. Furthermore, we demonstrate that audio-visual and other token types can be discarded once their information is transferred to LLM, with minimal impact on the model's prediction or even slight improvement, generalizing across multiple tasks and datasets, enabling more efficient inference. These findings hold across multiple models and scales, Qwen2.5-Omni and Video-SALMONN2 Plus at 3B and 7B scales, leading to hypotheses on why these flow structures emerge. Together, these results deliver the first coherent picture of how AVLLMs orchestrate sound and sight inside the network and lay the groundwork for the next wave of interpretability, design, and efficiency advances in audio-visual and broader MLLMs.

summary: Purchased artificial intelligence (AI) inference belongs in Scope 3 Category 1 of a corporate greenhouse gas inventory, yet practice omits it or applies a spend-based factor that gives 1.7 to 12.3 times the physical estimate and cannot tell one model or region from another. This paper sets out a token-based method and open dataset: a cradle-to-gate boundary, four tiers of activity data, an effective-token basis, a four-term factor (serving electricity, embodied hardware, data-centre construction, disclosed final training runs) and a rule resolving any model identifier and region to a factor. Inference footprints span twelve times between model classes and nine between regions. The mid-class factor, 0.039 kg of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) per million billed tokens at the world-average grid, is the low end of a stated structural range: a less efficient serving configuration raises it 2.8 times, and replacing the training term with all model development, on its own boundary, gives 1.5 to 2.9 times it. Input bands alone give -18% to +29%. Published per-query energy estimates that can describe a mid-class model are 2.4 to 7.2 times the mid-class energy, above its structural range in four of five rows; those that can describe a frontier-class model bracket it at 0.7 to 1.6 times. Worked examples give 8.5 kg CO2e a year for a 200-person firm, and 2.1 tonnes for fifty developers using agentic coding tools on a mid-class model or 8.3 tonnes on a frontier-class one. The contribution is a traceable figure; accuracy against metered energy is untested.

title: Context-Aware Multimodal Claim Verification in Spoken Dialogues
comments: Published at SALMA 2026 (EMNLP workshop). ACL Anthology: https://aclanthology.org/2026.salma-1.12/
summary: Spoken factual claims often occur within multi-turn conversations, where surrounding dialogue can provide context unavailable from the claim alone. Yet most fact-checking research evaluates isolated text, leaving conversational audio under-studied. We introduce MAD2, a synthetic Multi-turn Audio Dialogues benchmark for spoken claim verification with 1,000 two-speaker dialogues, 1,230 sentence-level check-worthy candidate annotations, and approximately 10 hours of audio. We also propose calibrated multimodal fusion of a context-aware audio encoder and a dialogue-aware text model. Adding dialogue context improves verification across settings, although the gains vary by scenario. Past-only context often approaches local offline performance, suggesting its usefulness when future context is unavailable. Fusion achieves its highest mean advantage over text with full-dialogue context, but does not consistently or significantly outperform text across settings. Under full-dialogue context, exploratory subgroup results show greater performance variation across dialogue scenarios for text and fusion, but across spread styles for audio.

title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding Can Jailbreak LLMs into Generating Malicious Code
summary:
Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for code generation, raising concerns that they may be misused to produce malicious code. Meanwhile, Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD) has been widely adopted to improve the reliability of LLM-generated code by enforcing syntactic validity. In this paper, we reveal a counterintuitive risk: this reliability-oriented technique can itself become an attack surface. We uncover a new jailbreak attack, termed CodeSpear, that exploits GCD to induce LLMs into generating malicious code. Our experiments show that simply applying a benign code grammar constraint can effectively jailbreak LLMs.
  To address this vulnerability, we propose CodeShield, a safety alignment approach that robustly preserves safe behavior even under attacker-controlled grammar constraints. CodeShield aligns the model in the code modality by teaching it to generate honeypot code under GCD. Such code is semantically harmless, so it does not implement the malicious request, and structurally diverse, so it is difficult to suppress through grammar tightening. At the same time, CodeShield still preserves natural-language refusals when natural language is available. Experiments on 10 popular LLMs across 4 benchmarks show that CodeSpear outperforms representative jailbreak baselines and increases the attack success rate by more than 30 percentage points on average. CodeShield also restores safety under CodeSpear while preserving benign utility. Our findings reveal a fundamental risk of GCD and call for greater attention to its potential security implications.

title: Jaguar: Fast Private Neural Network Inference with Power-of-Two Homomorphic Arithmetic
summary: Hybrid HE/2PC private neural network inference remains bottlenecked by prime-modulus homomorphic arithmetic in convolution and by a precision flow that runs ReLU at doubled bitwidth before invoking a separate truncation protocol. We present Jaguar, a system built on a single design choice--a power-of-two ciphertext ring--that addresses both. The choice enables SPA-Conv, a coefficient-domain convolution kernel that replaces NTT-centric polynomial multiplication with Scalar-Polynomial Accumulation, and an exact ciphertext-side truncation by local right shifts that lets ReLU run directly at the target fixed-point precision and eliminates the post-ReLU truncation protocol. Where NTT remains genuinely useful--at the client, for the single polynomial multiplication during decryption--we recover it through an auxiliary NTT prime, preserving the power-of-two protocol substrate while keeping decryption O(N log N). On ImageNet-scale ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and MobileNetV2 with AVX disabled, Jaguar achieves 2.07-3.72x lower end-to-end latency than Cheetah and 2.16-3.36x lower than Rhombus, with 1.16-1.76x lower communication than Cheetah.

title: DuoBench: A Reproducible Benchmark for Bimanual Manipulation in Simulation and the Real World
summary: Bimanual robot systems substantially expand manipulation capabilities, but coordinating two arms introduces additional control complexity and failure modes that are not well captured by existing benchmarks. We introduce DuoBench, an extensible benchmarking framework for bimanual manipulation policies on the FR3 Duo platform. DuoBench comprises eleven tasks spanning four coordination categories, implemented in simulation and partially replicated in the real world through reproducible task recipes with 3D-printable assets. In addition, we propose a stage-based evaluation scheme that supports fine-grained semantic failure analysis beyond binary success. It includes stage-conditional pass rates with confidence intervals as well as human-teleoperated datasets for all benchmark tasks. We benchmark several imitation-learning and vision-language-action policies in simulation and on real hardware. Our results show that current policies remain challenged by bimanual manipulation, particularly at the beginning of interaction, during parallel arm execution, and in sim-to-real transfer settings. We further find that simulation reveals the same failure modes as real-world experiments. DuoBench provides a reproducible testbed for analyzing them and studying future methods for dual-arm policy learning. Code, datasets, and videos are available at https://duobench.github.io

title: CVE-Conditioned Exploit Generation with LLMs: A Data-Centric Study of Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning
summary: We study the task of CVE-conditioned exploit generation, where a model drafts proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits given software vulnerability context. We adopt a data-centric approach, constructing a high-quality dataset via multi-stage preprocessing and introducing a scalable evaluation framework with LLM-as-judge and fine-grained rubrics. Under this unified setup, we benchmark 17 large language models across 8 evaluation criteria, providing systematic insights into their zero-shot capabilities. We further show that a compact 8B open-weight model, when fine-tuned on curated data, achieves over 42.5% improvement in exploit quality and rivals some proprietary models when combined with simple test-time rejection strategies. Our results highlight the importance of data quality, structured supervision, and evaluation design for reliable exploit generation, suggesting that these factors can be as critical as model scale in adapting LLMs to cybersecurity tasks.

title: Robust Learning under Non-Gaussian Noise with Adaptive Log-Correntropy Loss
summary: Robust deep learning under heavy-tailed and impulsive noise remains challenging because conventional losses such as mean squared error (MSE) exhibit unbounded sensitivity to outliers. Although correntropy-based objectives improve robustness, many conventional formulations rely on fixed kernel parameters that must be empirically tuned and remain static during training. To address these limitations, we propose an Adaptive Log-Correntropy Loss (ALCL), a heavy-tailed loss formulation that adaptively learns its robustness geometry during optimization. ALCL introduces a logarithmic residual model whose shape and scale parameters are learned jointly with network weights through differentiable reparameterization. This yields a heavy-tailed robust optimization objective whose psi-function is formally bounded and redescending, allowing the loss geometry to adapt dynamically to evolving residual statistics while suppressing extreme outliers. Comparative experiments on four widely used benchmark datasets spanning grayscale and red-green-blue (RGB) image data under mixed heavy-tailed and impulsive noise demonstrate that ALCL consistently outperforms MSE and optimally tuned generalized correntropy losses in both reconstruction fidelity and downstream classification accuracy. While performance differences remain small under low-noise conditions, under high-noise regimes ALCL improves median accuracy by up to 4.75% on grayscale benchmarks and 4.51% on RGB datasets, with reduced variance across runs. These results demonstrate that adaptive robustness through joint learning of loss parameters provides a computationally efficient alternative to static correntropy-based losses for deep learning in non-Gaussian environments.

AI.result: 在四个基准数据集上的实验表明，ALCL在混合重尾和脉冲噪声下，在重建保真度和下游分类准确性方面，始终优于均方误差和经过优化的广义相关熵损失。在高噪声情况下，ALCL将中位数准确率在中值图像数据集上提高了多达4.75%，在RGB数据集上提高了4.51%，同时降低了运行方差。
AI.conclusion: 通过联合学习损失参数实现自适应鲁棒性，为在非高斯环境下进行深度学习提供了一种比静态相关熵损失更具计算效率的替代方案。
AI.translation: 在非高斯噪声下进行鲁棒的深度学习，特别是处理重尾和脉冲噪声，仍然是一个挑战，因为像均方误差（MSE）这样的传统损失函数对异常值表现出无限的敏感性。尽管基于相关熵的目标提高了鲁棒性，但许多传统公式依赖于需要经验调整且在训练期间保持静态的固定核参数。为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了一种自适应对数相关熵损失（ALCL），这是一种重尾损失公式，可在优化过程中自适应地学习其鲁棒性几何形状。ALCL引入了一个对数残差模型，其形状和尺度参数通过可微分重参数化与网络权重联合学习。这产生了一个重尾鲁棒优化目标，其psi函数在形式上是有界的且是红色的，允许损失几何动态地适应不断变化的残差统计，同时抑制极端异常值。在跨越灰度级和红-绿-蓝（RGB）图像数据、混合重尾和脉冲噪声的四个广泛使用的基准数据集上的比较实验表明，ALCL在重建保真度和下游分类准确性方面，始终优于MSE和经过最优调整的广义相关熵损失。虽然在低噪声条件下性能差异很小，但在高噪声环境下，ALCL将灰度级基准数据集上的中位数准确率提高了多达4.75%，在RGB数据集上提高了4.51%，并且运行方差减小。这些结果表明，通过联合学习损失参数实现的自适应鲁棒性，为在非高斯环境下的深度学习提供了一种比静态相关熵损失更具计算效率的替代方案。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种自适应对数相关熵损失（ALCL），用于解决深度学习中由非高斯噪声（特别是重尾和脉冲噪声）引起的问题。与传统的对异常值敏感的损失函数（如MSE）以及需要手动调整参数的现有相关熵损失不同，ALCL能够通过联合学习网络权重和损失函数的形状/尺度参数，动态地适应噪声环境。实验证明，ALCL在重建和分类任务中均优于现有方法，尤其在高噪声条件下表现显著，同时降低了结果的方差。
AI.keywords: 自适应对数相关熵损失, 鲁棒学习, 非高斯噪声, 重尾噪声, 深度学习
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的自适应损失函数ALCL，解决了现有鲁棒学习方法在处理非高斯噪声时的局限性。通过联合学习损失函数参数，ALCL能够动态调整其鲁棒性，这在理论和实践上都有重要意义。然而，计算效率的提升以及在大规模、多样化数据集上的进一步验证将是未来研究的重点。

title: Sparse stochastic digital twins can outperform exact ones
summary: Digital twins are often built under the assumption that greater model fidelity leads to better downstream performance. We show that this is not always the case: retaining weakly dependent or auxiliary degrees of freedom can increase the dimensionality of learning and control problems enough that a sparse stochastic surrogate outperforms even an exact high-dimensional model. To identify such structure, we introduce a framework for dependence discovery directly at the level of the full conditional law. The method combines conditional generative modeling with Gaussian-process distillation and kernel mode decomposition to quantify how strongly individual variables enter the conditional distribution, including through variability, tails, multimodality, and other features invisible to the conditional mean. The resulting dependence structure can be used both to construct sparse stochastic digital twins from data and to reduce known high-dimensional models for downstream tasks. In a modified Lunar Lander problem, an eight-dimensional sparse surrogate yields better control performance than the exact 109-dimensional simulator despite lower transition fidelity. A stochastic heat-equation example shows that the framework recovers sparse structure in a 102-dimensional data-driven setting and produces a more effective surrogate than one conditioned on all candidate inputs, while economic data demonstrate its use for identifying time-varying memory structure. These results show that model fidelity and downstream utility are distinct objectives, and that dependence discovery provides a practical route to sparse stochastic digital twins.

AI.title_translation: 稀疏随机数字孪生可以超越精确孪生
AI.tldr: 研究表明，保留弱相关或辅助自由度会增加学习和控制问题的维度，导致稀疏随机模型在某些情况下优于精确高维模型。通过一种新的依赖性发现框架，可以构建稀疏随机数字孪生，并在示例中证明其优越性。
AI.motivation: 数字孪生通常假设更高的模型保真度能带来更好的下游性能，但该研究表明事实并非总是如此，保留弱相关或辅助自由度可能导致稀疏随机模型优于精确模型。
AI.method: 提出了一种直接在完整条件律层面进行依赖性发现的框架，结合了条件生成模型、高斯过程蒸馏和核模式分解，以量化变量对条件分布的贡献，并据此构建稀疏随机数字孪生或简化已知模型。
AI.result: 在改进的月球着陆器问题中，一个八维稀疏模型在控制性能上优于精确的109维模拟器。在随机热方程示例中，该框架成功地从102维数据中恢复了稀疏结构，并生成了比基于所有候选输入条件化的模型更有效的替代模型。经济数据也展示了其识别时变记忆结构的能力。
AI.conclusion: 模型保真度和下游效用是不同的目标，依赖性发现为构建稀疏随机数字孪生提供了一条实用途径。
AI.translation: 数字孪生通常在更高的模型保真度会带来更好的下游性能的假设下构建。我们表明，情况并非总是如此：保留弱相关或辅助自由度会增加学习和控制问题的维度，以至于稀疏随机替代模型甚至优于精确的高维模型。为了识别这种结构，我们引入了一个直接在完整条件律层面进行依赖性发现的框架。该方法结合了条件生成建模、高斯过程蒸馏和核模式分解，以量化单个变量如何通过变异性、尾部、多模态性和其他条件均值无法察觉的特征，强烈地进入条件分布。由此产生的依赖性结构既可用于从数据构建稀疏随机数字孪生，也可用于为下游任务简化已知的高维模型。在改进的月球着陆器问题中，一个八维稀疏替代模型产生的控制性能优于精确的109维模拟器，尽管其转换保真度较低。一个随机热方程示例表明，该框架在102维数据驱动设置中恢复了稀疏结构，并产生了比基于所有候选输入条件化的替代模型更有效的替代模型，而经济数据则展示了其在识别时变记忆结构方面的应用。这些结果表明，模型保真度和下游效用是不同的目标，并且依赖性发现为稀疏随机数字孪生提供了一条实用途径。
AI.summary: 该研究挑战了数字孪生模型保真度越高越好的传统观点，提出稀疏随机数字孪生在某些情况下可能优于精确模型。研究人员开发了一种新的依赖性发现框架，通过分析变量的完整条件律来识别关键结构，并成功构建了稀疏随机数字孪生。实验结果表明，该方法在月球着陆器控制、热方程模拟和经济数据分析等多个领域均表现出优越性能，证明了模型保真度和下游效用是独立的目标，并且依赖性发现是实现高效稀疏数字孪生的有效途径。
AI.keywords: 数字孪生, 稀疏模型, 依赖性发现, 条件律, 模型保真度, 下游效用, 随机替代模型, 核模式分解, 高斯过程蒸馏, 条件生成模型, 月球着陆器, 热方程, 经济数据
AI.comments: 这项研究提出了一个重要的观点，即在数字孪生领域，模型保真度和下游任务的效用之间可能存在权衡。所提出的依赖性发现框架具有创新性，它能够超越传统的条件均值分析，捕捉更丰富的变量间依赖关系。然而，该框架的计算复杂度和在不同类型数据上的泛化能力仍需进一步研究。此外，如何将这种稀疏表示有效地整合到现有的数字孪生构建流程中也是一个值得探讨的问题。

title: Agent trajectories as programs: fingerprinting and programming coding-agent behavior
summary: Benchmark scores tell you what an agent got right; they do not tell you how it got there. In this work, we introduce methods for comparing agents procedurally in different contexts, where the model, tasks, and approaches vary. We compare ten agents and find that they are identifiable by their behavioral habits, which we define as fingerprints: a probe over these procedural signatures attributes an unseen trajectory to the correct agent at 85.7% accuracy. We develop procedural representations for agent problem-solving procedures with an emergent vocabulary induction technique which is meant to be maximally compressive to avoid surface-level variation while being expressive enough to unveil the quirks of the models' patterns. We apply our framework to the software engineering evaluation dataset SWE-Bench to study the structural distinctness of agent trajectories and find that behavior is most similar between models from similar release periods and those that are distilled from one another (e.g., a distilled student model and its teacher have a Jensen-Shannon divergence of 0.25, about half the distance between other model pairs). As more models saturate evaluations, we believe that it will be important to probe model behavior along more holistic dimensions than success rates alone. We introduce ProcGrep, a library for auditing and evaluating agents for how they approach tasks at a procedural level given their traces in a top-down fashion. ProcGrep is available at https://github.com/hamidahoderinwale/procgrep.

AI.title_translation: Agent Trajectories as Programs: Fingerprinting and Programming Coding-Agent Behavior
AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new method to compare AI agents based on their problem-solving procedures, not just their final scores. They found agents have unique 'fingerprints' based on their behavior patterns, allowing them to be identified with high accuracy. This method can also reveal relationships between agents, like those based on similar release dates or teacher-student models. A library called ProcGrep is provided to audit agent behavior at a procedural level.
AI.motivation: Benchmark scores alone do not explain how AI agents arrive at their solutions. There is a need for methods to compare agents procedurally across different models, tasks, and approaches to understand their behavior and problem-solving strategies.
AI.method: The researchers developed a method to represent agent problem-solving procedures using an emergent vocabulary induction technique. This technique aims to be compressive and avoid surface-level variations while highlighting unique model patterns. They used this to create 'fingerprints' of agent behavior and applied it to the SWE-Bench dataset. They also introduced a library called ProcGrep for auditing and evaluating agents based on their traces.
AI.result: Agents were found to be identifiable by their behavioral habits or 'fingerprints,' with an unseen trajectory being attributed to the correct agent with 85.7% accuracy. Behavior similarity was highest between models from similar release periods or those distilled from each other (e.g., teacher-student models had a Jensen-Shannon divergence of 0.25).
AI.conclusion: As AI model evaluations become more saturated, it's crucial to assess model behavior beyond just success rates, considering more holistic dimensions. The proposed procedural analysis and the ProcGrep library offer a way to audit and evaluate agents based on their task-solving approaches.
AI.translation: 基准分数告诉你代理在哪些方面做得对；它们并不能告诉你它是如何做到的。在本研究中，我们引入了在不同环境、模型、任务和方法变化的情况下程序化地比较代理的方法。我们比较了十个代理，发现它们可以通过它们的行为习惯来识别，我们将其定义为指纹：对这些程序化签名的探测能够以 85.7% 的准确率将未见过的轨迹归因于正确的代理。我们开发了用于代理问题解决程序的程序化表示，并采用了一种旨在最大程度压缩以避免表面变化但又足够表达以揭示模型模式怪癖的涌现词汇归纳技术。我们将我们的框架应用于软件工程评估数据集 SWE-Bench，以研究代理轨迹的结构独特性，并发现行为在相似发布时期的模型之间以及相互蒸馏的模型之间最为相似（例如，蒸馏的学生模型和它的老师之间的 Jensen-Shannon 散度为 0.25，大约是其他模型对之间距离的一半）。随着越来越多的模型充斥评估，我们相信，除了成功率之外，探究模型行为的更全面的维度将变得很重要。我们引入了 ProcGrep，这是一个用于从顶层审计和评估代理在给定其轨迹的任务处理方式的库。ProcGrep 可在 https://github.com/hamidahoderinwale/procgrep 获取。
AI.summary: This paper introduces a novel approach to analyze and compare AI agents by examining their problem-solving procedures, termed 'fingerprints,' rather than solely relying on benchmark scores. The method uses emergent vocabulary induction to create compressive yet expressive representations of agent behavior. Experiments on ten agents demonstrated that these behavioral fingerprints allow for accurate identification (85.7%) of unseen trajectories. The study also found that agent behavior correlates with release periods and distillation relationships. A new library, ProcGrep, is presented for auditing agent behavior at a procedural level, advocating for a more holistic evaluation of AI agents beyond success rates.
AI.keywords: agent behavior, procedural analysis, trajectory fingerprinting, ProcGrep, emergent vocabulary induction
AI.comments: The paper presents an innovative approach to understanding AI agent behavior by focusing on the process rather than just the outcome. The concept of 'fingerprinting' agent trajectories is compelling and offers a more nuanced evaluation method. The development of ProcGrep is a valuable contribution for researchers in this field. A potential limitation could be the computational cost of generating and analyzing these procedural representations, especially for very complex agents or long trajectories. Future work could explore the generalizability of these fingerprints across vastly different domains.

title: Rethinking Dataset Distillation for Classification: Do Distilled Sets Outperform Coresets?
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Track on Evaluations and Datasets
summary: Dataset distillation (DD) has emerged as a prominent approach in data centric machine learning, aiming to synthesize compact training sets for efficient training by compressing the information in large datasets into a small number of synthetic samples. However, DD methods are often evaluated under inconsistent evaluation protocols, ranging from standard ERM to single/multi-teacher supervision, making it difficult to isolate the effectiveness of distilled data from evaluation. Moreover, many prior methods claim that DD outperforms data pruning approaches such as coreset selection (CS), based on the assumption that restricting condensed datasets to subsets of real samples fundamentally limits their expressiveness. In this work, we critically evaluate DD methods through large-scale experiments using standardized datasets and evaluation protocols to assess their intrinsic effectiveness. We benchmark seven state-of-the-art (SOTA) DD methods on ImageNet-1K, ImageNet100, and ImageNette, using three widely adopted training protocols against four CS strategies. Our results show that while some DD methods fail to outperform even simple random subsets, the SOTA DD approaches are comparable to or worse than coresets on large-scale datasets and incur a substantially higher cost for construction. Beyond accuracy, we also evaluate the representativeness, diversity, and quality of condensed sets, and find that coresets consistently achieve better coverage of the original data distribution. These findings highlight the limited practical advantages of current DD methods and show that coresets remain competitive and are often a more computationally efficient alternative for data-centric learning.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Track on Evaluations and Datasets

AI.title_translation: 分类数据集蒸馏的再思考：蒸馏集是否优于核心集？
AI.tldr: 数据集蒸馏（DD）旨在合成紧凑的训练集，但其有效性评估不一致。本文通过大规模实验对DD方法进行了批判性评估，发现在大型数据集上，DD方法通常不优于或劣于核心集（CS），且构建成本更高。核心集在代表性、多样性和质量方面表现更好，并且在计算效率上更具优势。
AI.motivation: 现有数据集蒸馏（DD）方法评估协议不一致，难以分离蒸馏数据本身的有效性。许多先前的方法声称DD优于数据剪枝方法（如核心集选择CS），但这种说法是在特定假设下得出的。本文旨在通过大规模实验，使用标准化的数据集和评估协议，批判性地评估DD方法的内在有效性。
AI.method: 在ImageNet-1K、ImageNet100和ImageNette数据集上，使用三种广泛采用的训练协议，对七种最先进（SOTA）的DD方法与四种CS策略进行了基准测试。除了准确性，还评估了精简数据集的代表性、多样性和质量。
AI.result: 部分DD方法甚至未能优于简单的随机子集。在大型数据集上，SOTA的DD方法在性能上与核心集相当或更差，并且在构建成本上显著更高。核心集在代表性、多样性和质量方面始终能更好地覆盖原始数据分布。
AI.conclusion: 现有DD方法在实际应用中的优势有限，而核心集在数据中心学习中仍然具有竞争力，并且通常是更具计算效率的选择。
AI.translation: 数据集蒸馏（DD）已成为数据中心机器学习中的一种重要方法，旨在通过将大型数据集的信息压缩成少量合成样本来合成紧凑的训练集，以实现高效训练。然而，DD方法的评估通常在不一致的评估协议下进行，从标准的ERM到单/多教师监督不等，这使得人们很难将蒸馏数据的有效性与评估分离开来。此外，许多先前的方法声称DD优于数据剪枝方法，如核心集选择（CS），其前提是假设将精简数据集限制为真实样本的子集会从根本上限制其表达能力。在本研究中，我们通过使用标准化的数据集和评估协议进行大规模实验，批判性地评估DD方法，以评估其内在有效性。我们在ImageNet-1K、ImageNet100和ImageNette上，使用三种广泛采用的训练协议，针对四种CS策略，对七种最先进（SOTA）的DD方法进行了基准测试。我们的结果表明，虽然一些DD方法未能优于简单的随机子集，但在大型数据集上，SOTA的DD方法与核心集相当或更差，并且其构建成本也高得多。除了准确性之外，我们还评估了精简数据集的代表性、多样性和质量，发现核心集在覆盖原始数据分布方面始终表现更好。这些发现凸显了当前DD方法的实际优势有限，并表明核心集在数据中心学习中仍然具有竞争力，而且通常是更具计算效率的替代方案。
AI.summary: 本文批判性地评估了数据集蒸馏（DD）方法，发现其在大型数据集上的性能通常不优于或劣于核心集（CS），且构建成本更高。研究表明，核心集在数据代表性、多样性和质量方面表现更佳，并且在计算效率上更具优势，因此在数据中心学习中是更具竞争力的选择。
AI.keywords: 数据集蒸馏, 核心集, 数据中心学习, 数据压缩, 评估协议
AI.comments: 该研究对数据集蒸馏（DD）领域的现状提出了重要的质疑。通过严格的实验设计和大规模数据集的评估，研究者揭示了许多DD方法可能存在的过度宣传和评估偏差问题。研究结果强调了在比较不同数据压缩技术时，标准化评估协议和计算成本的重要性。此外，研究为核心集（CS）作为一种更具成本效益和性能的替代方案提供了有力的证据，这可能对未来的数据中心学习研究和实践产生重要影响。然而，研究也可能存在局限性，例如可能未涵盖所有最新的DD方法，或者实验设置可能无法完全模拟所有实际应用场景。

title: RTSGameBench: Evaluating VLMs for Strategic Reasoning in Game Environments
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) often struggle with strategic reasoning in a multi-agent setting, i.e., deciding under uncertainty while coordinating with and adapting to other agents. Real-time strategy (RTS) games can be a natural testbed for this capability, requiring long-horizon planning, coordination with allies, and adaptation to opponents under partial observability. But existing RTS benchmarks cover limited agent configurations, lack controlled evaluation across distinct strategic demands, and remain confined to fixed scenarios. To address these gaps, we propose RTSGAMEBENCH, built on Beyond All Reason, an RTS game whose larger scale broadens the strategic space beyond prior testbeds. In RTSGAMEBENCH, we offer holistic evaluation across diverse full-game matchups, diagnostic mini-games each emphasizing a focal strategic demand, and extensible coverage via a self-evolving framework that turns free-form queries into new mini-games, improving with accumulated experience. We further propose RTSGAMEAGENT, an agent harness that combines scalable group-level trajectory planning with short- and long-term memory and outperforms existing agents. We find that state-of-the-art VLMs struggle where humans succeed, particularly when they must coordinate with allies or contend with multiple opponents.

AI.title_translation: RTSGameBench：在游戏环境中评估多模态大模型的战略推理能力
AI.tldr: 本文推出了RTSGAMEBENCH，用于评估视觉-语言模型在复杂即时战略游戏中的多智能体战略推理与规划能力。
AI.motivation: 现有的视觉-语言模型（VLM）在多智能体环境中的战略推理能力（如在不确定性下决策、协调和适应其他智能体）方面表现不佳。虽然即时战略（RTS）游戏是测试这种能力的理想环境，但现有的RTS基准测试存在智能体配置受限、缺乏针对不同战略需求的对照评估以及场景固定的问题。
AI.method: 提出了RTSGAMEBENCH基准测试（包含全游戏对局、诊断性小游戏以及基于自进化框架的可扩展覆盖），并设计了RTSGAMEAGENT智能体架构（结合了可扩展的群体级轨迹规划与短期/长期记忆）。
AI.result: RTSGAMEAGENT的性能优于现有智能体；实验发现，最先进的VLM在人类擅长的领域（特别是需要与盟友协调或应对多对手时）表现出明显的不足。
AI.conclusion: 现有的最先进VLM在需要盟友协作或应对多个对手的即时战略游戏中表现不佳，远远落后于人类，这表明多模态大模型在复杂战略推理和多智能体协同方面仍有很大提升空间。
AI.translation: 视觉-语言模型（VLM）在多智能体环境中的战略推理方面往往表现不佳，即在不确定性下进行决策，同时与其他智能体进行协调和适应。实时战略（RTS）游戏可以作为这种能力的天然测试平台，需要长期的规划、与盟友的协调以及在部分可观测性下对对手的适应。然而，现有的RTS基准测试涵盖有限的智能体配置，缺乏对不同战略需求的对照评估，并且局限于固定场景。为了解决这些空白，我们提出了RTSGAMEBENCH，它建立在《Beyond All Reason》（一款RTS游戏）之上，其更大的规模扩展了先前测试平台之外的战略空间。在RTSGAMEBENCH中，我们提供全面的评估，包括多样化的完整游戏对局、强调核心战略需求的诊断性小游戏，以及通过自我进化框架实现的可扩展覆盖（该框架将自由形式的查询转化为新的小游戏，并随着积累的经验而改进）。我们进一步提出了RTSGAMEAGENT，这是一种结合了可扩展的群体级轨迹规划与短长期记忆的智能体框架，其表现优于现有智能体。我们发现，最先进的VLM在人类成功的地方往往举步维艰，特别是当它们必须与盟友协调或应对多个对手时。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了RTSGAMEBENCH，一个基于大型RTS游戏《Beyond All Reason》的基准测试，用于全面评估视觉-语言模型（VLM）在多智能体战略推理中的表现。同时，文章还提出了RTSGAMEAGENT智能体架构，实验结果表明当前VLM在处理复杂的盟友协作和多对手对抗等战略场景时仍面临巨大挑战。
AI.keywords: Vision-Language Models, Real-Time Strategy Games, Strategic Reasoning, Multi-Agent Systems, Benchmark
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地引入了大规模即时战略游戏环境来评估多模态大模型（VLM）在复杂多智能体设定下的战略推理能力，通过综合的基准测试、诊断性小游戏以及自进化框架，填补了现有测试的空白。这对理解和提升VLM在不确定性、长期规划及多方协同方面的能力具有重要意义。

title: Nearly Optimal Submodular Sparsification, with and without Cardinality Constraints
summary: We study the sparsification of decomposable submodular functions: given a sum $F(S) = \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(S)$ of $m$ nonnegative submodular functions on an $n$-element ground set $[n]$ (without assuming monotonicity or symmetry), the goal is to find a sparse reweighting $\widetilde{F}(S) = \sum_{i=1}^m w_i f_i(S)$ with at most $s \ll m$ nonzero weights that preserves $F(S)$ within a $(1 \pm \varepsilon)$ factor across a target family of queries. For all subset queries $S \subseteq [n]$, we give a polynomial-time randomized algorithm that constructs a sparsifier of size $O(n^2 \log n / \varepsilon^2)$. This improves upon the previous best upper bound of $O(n^3 / \varepsilon^2)$ by Kenneth and Krauthgamer and resolves their open conjecture up to a logarithmic factor, matching the $Ω(n^2)$ lower bound from directed cuts. Motivated by capacity budgets in submodular applications and the Restricted Isometry Property (RIP) in compressed sensing, we further study submodular sparsification under a cardinality constraint $|S| \le k$, and obtain a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs a sparsifier of size $O(n k \log n / \varepsilon^2)$, nearly matching the $Ω(nk)$ lower bound. This shows that a cardinality constraint unconditionally reduces the size of general submodular sparsifiers by a factor of roughly $k/n$; we complement this with $Ω(n)$ lower bounds showing that even regular symmetric or almost-regular monotone submodular functions cannot be sparsified to $o(n)$ size for $k = 2$ and $k = 1$, respectively.

AI.title_translation: 近乎最优的可分子模稀疏化，带或不带基数约束
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了用于可分子模函数稀疏化的算法，在没有基数约束时，将稀疏度提升至O(n^2 log n / ε^2)；在有基数约束时，将稀疏度提升至O(nk log n / ε^2)，均接近理论下界。
AI.motivation: 为了在子模应用中处理容量预算和压缩感知中的RIP问题，研究了带基数约束的子模稀疏化问题。
AI.method: 提出了一种多项式时间随机算法，用于构建子模稀疏化器。
AI.result: 在没有基数约束的情况下，算法构建了一个大小为O(n^2 log n / ε^2)的稀疏化器，优于先前O(n^3 / ε^2)的上限。在有基数约束的情况下，算法构建了一个大小为O(nk log n / ε^2)的稀疏化器，接近Ω(nk)的下限。
AI.conclusion: 该研究成功地提出了用于可分子模函数稀疏化的算法，并在没有和有基数约束的情况下都取得了接近理论下界的性能。研究结果表明，基数约束可以将一般子模稀疏器的规模无条件地减小大约k/n的因子。
AI.translation: 我们研究可分子模函数的稀疏化：给定一个由n个元素的基集[n]上的m个非负子模函数组成的和F(S) = Σ_{i=1}^m f_i(S)（不假设单调性或对称性），目标是找到一个稀疏重加权F~(S) = Σ_{i=1}^m w_i f_i(S)，其中非零权重最多为s << m，在目标查询族上将F(S)保持在(1±ε)因子内。对于所有子集查询S⊆[n]，我们提供了一个多项式时间随机算法，该算法构造了一个大小为O(n^2 log n / ε^2)的稀疏化器。这优于Kenneth和Krauthgamer先前O(n^3 / ε^2)的最佳上限，并解决了他们开放的猜想（相差一个对数因子），匹配了来自有向割的Ω(n^2)下界。受子模应用中容量预算和压缩感知中受限等距性质（RIP）的启发，我们进一步研究了基数约束|S|≤k下的子模稀疏化，并获得了一个多项式时间算法，该算法构造了一个大小为O(nk log n / ε^2)的稀疏化器，接近Ω(nk)的下限。这表明基数约束无条件地将一般子模稀疏器的规模减小了大约k/n的因子；我们通过Ω(n)的下界来补充这一点，表明即使是正则对称或几乎正则单调子模函数，对于k=2和k=1，也无法稀疏到o(n)的大小。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种用于稀疏化可分子模函数（可能非单调或非对称）的算法。在没有基数约束的情况下，算法将稀疏化器的尺寸从之前的O(n^3 / ε^2)改进到O(n^2 log n / ε^2)，接近Ω(n^2)的下界。在存在基数约束（最多k个元素）的情况下，算法构造了一个尺寸为O(nk log n / ε^2)的稀疏化器，接近Ω(nk)的下界，并表明基数约束能显著减小稀疏化器的尺寸。
AI.keywords: 子模稀疏化, 基数约束, 随机算法, 压缩感知, 容量预算
AI.comments: 该研究在子模稀疏化领域取得了重要进展，特别是在处理非单调和非对称函数以及引入基数约束方面。算法在理论上取得了接近最优的性能，这对于实际应用具有重要意义。然而，算法的随机性质和对ε的依赖性可能在某些实际场景中需要进一步考虑。

title: WildBox: A Dataset and Benchmark for Aerial Monocular 3D Detection of African Savanna Wildlife
summary: We introduce WildBox, a dataset and benchmark for monocular 3D detection of wildlife from drone video, comprising 237,505 3D bounding box annotations across seven African savanna species grouped into six benchmark classes. Annotations follow a KITTI/Omni3D-compatible format in a per-segment scale-normalised camera frame, with instance identities maintained across each segment. We evaluate two open-vocabulary monocular 3D architectures, OVMono3D-LIFT and DetAny3D, under zero-shot, ground-truth 2D box prompt, and supervised fine-tuning protocols. Open-vocabulary 2D foundation models provide usable zero-shot wildlife localisation (50.55 AP@50), but zero-shot 3D detection collapses to 0.00 AP across both architectures and every 2D-input condition tested, including ground-truth 2D box prompts, thus isolating the failure to the 3D stage. Fine-tuning on WildBox recovers performance to 8.68 +/- 0.47 AP-BEV@0.50 and 13.17 +/- 0.69 AP3D macro. Depth contributes 84% of normalised Hausdorff distance after fine-tuning and over 99% in zero-shot, identifying monocular aerial depth as the dominant open problem in this regime. A coarse-to-fine curriculum, i.e. pretraining on a merged zebra class before fine-tuning on the Grevy's/plains split, improves macro 3D performance with less total compute, with the largest gains on the two zebra subclasses. WildBox is released with video-level splits and baseline checkpoints to enable progress in 3D wildlife perception from drone video.

AI.title_translation: WildBox：用于非洲大草原野生动物无人机单目3D检测的数据集与基准
AI.tldr: WildBox是首个针对无人机视频中非洲大草原野生动物的单目3D检测数据集和基准，揭示了深度估计是该领域的主要技术瓶颈，并通过微调和课程学习策略显著改善了检测性能。
AI.motivation: 弥补当前缺乏针对无人机视频中非洲大草原野生动物单目3D检测的公开数据集和基准的不足，评估并解决现有开放词汇2D/3D基础模型在该领域面临的挑战。
AI.method: 引入WildBox数据集，评估两种开放词汇单目3D架构（OVMono3D-LIFT和DetAny3D）在零样本、真实2D框提示和监督微调协议下的性能，并采用粗到精的课程学习策略进行预训练和微调。
AI.result: 零样本3D检测在所有架构和条件下均表现为0.00 AP，表明瓶颈在于3D阶段（尤其是深度估计）。通过微调可将性能恢复至8.68 AP-BEV和13.17 AP3D macro，而粗到精的课程学习策略进一步提升了宏观3D性能并减少了计算量。
AI.conclusion: WildBox为无人机视频中的野生动物单目3D检测提供了宝贵的数据集和基准。研究表明，单目 aerial 深度估计是当前的主要瓶颈，而通过微调和粗到精的课程学习可以显著提升3D检测性能。
AI.translation: 我们介绍了WildBox，这是一个用于无人机视频中野生动物单目3D检测的数据集和基准，包含分布在六个基准类别中的七种非洲大草原物种的237,505个3D边界框标注。标注遵循兼容KITTI/Omni3D的格式，采用每段尺度归一化的相机坐标系，并在每个视频段中保持实例身份。我们在零样本、真实2D框提示和监督微调协议下评估了两个开放词汇单目3D架构：OVMono3D-LIFT和DetAny3D。开放词汇2D基础模型提供了可用的零样本野生动物定位（50.55 AP@50），但零样本3D检测在所有架构和测试的2D输入条件下（包括真实2D框提示）均崩溃至0.00 AP，从而将失效根源隔离到了3D阶段。在WildBox上进行微调将性能恢复至8.68 +/- 0.47 AP-BEV@0.50和13.17 +/- 0.69 AP3D macro。微调后，深度占归一化豪斯多夫距离的84%，在零样本情况下超过99%，这表明单目 aerial 深度估计是该领域占主导地位的未解难题。一种粗到精的课程学习策略（即在合并的斑马类别上进行预训练，然后在细分的细斑马/平原斑马类别上进行微调）以更少的总计算量提高了宏观3D性能，并在两个斑马子类上获得了最大收益。WildBox随附视频级分割和基准检查点发布，以推动无人机视频3D野生动物感知技术的发展。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了WildBox，这是一个用于无人机视频中非洲大草原野生动物单目3D检测的数据集和基准，包含超过23万个3D边界框标注。研究评估了现有的开放词汇3D架构，发现单目深度估计是主要瓶颈，并通过监督微调和课程学习验证了性能的恢复与提升。
AI.keywords: 野生动物监测, 单目3D检测, 无人机视频, 数据集与基准, 开放世界视觉
AI.comments: 该论文填补了无人机视角下非洲大草原野生动物单目3D检测数据集和基准的空白，揭示了当前开放世界2D基础模型在3D阶段失效的原因（主要在于深度估计），并提出了有效的微调和课程学习策略，对生态保护和无人机视觉研究具有重要意义。

title: Radial Basis Function Networks as Projection Heads in Self-Supervised Learning
summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) typically relies on a backbone encoder followed by a small multilayer perceptron (MLP) projection head, which is conventionally discarded after training, while backbone quality is assessed via costly linear probing on labeled data. We argue that this approach including discarding the projector is rather computationally wasteful. Instead, we propose replacing the MLP head with a radial basis function network (RBFN), whose interpretable center and shape parameters can be exploited to judge representation quality without labels or a separate classifier. To this end, we introduce Scale-Normalized Separation (SNS), a novel label-free quality metric derived solely from the kernel centers and shapes learned during training. Across five canonical SSL architectures (MoCo, SimCLR, BYOL, SwAV and SimSiam) and four image classification datasets, we show that RBFN projection heads are competitive drop-in replacements for standard MLP projectors. We recommend constructing them with three RBF layers activated by the Gaussian radial basis function. Moreover, SNS exhibits strong to very strong positive correlation with established logistic regression metrics, demonstrating that a trained RBFN projector can act as a reliable proxy for backbone representation quality. We additionally publish a novel PyTorch compatible image classification dataset based on Google's Open Images V7 to facilitate reproducible research into representation learning.

AI.title_translation: 径向基函数网络作为自监督学习中的投影头
AI.tldr: 该研究提出用径向基函数网络（RBFN）取代自监督学习中常用的多层感知机（MLP）投影头，并引入了一种名为SNS的无标签质量评估指标，该指标仅基于RBFN学习到的核中心和形状。实验证明，RBFN作为投影头效果与MLP相当，并且SNS指标能有效评估表示质量，无需标签或单独的分类器。
AI.motivation: 传统的自监督学习方法在训练后丢弃投影头，并依赖昂贵的有标签线性探测来评估骨干网络的质量，这种方法计算成本高且浪费。因此，研究旨在探索更高效的表示质量评估方法。
AI.method: 将径向基函数网络（RBFN）作为投影头，并提出一种名为Scale-Normalized Separation（SNS）的无标签质量评估指标，该指标仅基于RBFN学习到的核中心和形状。在五种自监督学习架构和四个图像分类数据集上进行了实验。
AI.result: RBFN投影头在计算性能上与标准的MLP投影头相当，并且SNS指标与传统的逻辑回归评估指标显示出强烈的正相关性，证明了RBFN投影头可以作为骨干表示质量的可靠代理。研究还发布了一个新的基于Open Images V7的图像分类数据集以促进可重复性研究。
AI.conclusion: 径向基函数网络（RBFN）可以作为自监督学习中MLP投影头的有效替代品，并且基于RBFN学习到的参数（核中心和形状）可以推导出SNS这一新的无标签质量评估指标，用于可靠地评估表示质量，从而避免了传统的有标签线性探测的计算成本。
AI.translation: 自监督学习（SSL）通常依赖于骨干编码器，然后是一个小型多层感知机（MLP）投影头，该投影头在训练后通常被丢弃，而骨干网络的质量则通过有标签数据的线性探测进行评估。我们认为，包括丢弃投影头在内的方法在计算上是浪费的。因此，我们提出用径向基函数网络（RBFN）取代MLP头，其可解释的中心和形状参数可以用来在没有标签或单独的分类器的情况下判断表示质量。为此，我们引入了Scale-Normalized Separation（SNS），这是一种新颖的无标签质量指标，仅从训练过程中学到的核中心和形状推导出来。在五种典型的SSL架构（MoCo、SimCLR、BYOL、SwAV和SimSiam）和四个图像分类数据集上，我们表明RBFN投影头是标准MLP投影头的有竞争力的即插即用替代品。我们推荐使用高斯径向基函数激活的三个RBF层来构建它们。此外，SNS与已建立的逻辑回归指标显示出强到非常强的正相关性，证明了训练好的RBFN投影头可以作为骨干表示质量的可靠代理。我们还发布了一个基于Google Open Images V7的新型PyTorch兼容图像分类数据集，以促进表示学习的可重复性研究。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种新颖的自监督学习方法，用径向基函数网络（RBFN）取代传统的MLP投影头，并引入了Scale-Normalized Separation（SNS）这一无标签质量评估指标。实验结果表明，RBFN投影头在性能上可与MLP媲美，而SNS指标能够有效且无需标签地评估表示质量，为自监督学习的评估提供了一种更高效的途径。
AI.keywords: 径向基函数网络,自监督学习,投影头,表示质量评估,Scale-Normalized Separation
AI.comments: 这项研究提出了一个有趣且实用的方法，将RBFN应用于自监督学习的投影头，并引入了SNS这一创新的无标签评估指标。这种方法不仅在计算效率上有所提升，而且提供了对表示质量的新见解。然而，RBFN的计算复杂度与MLP相比可能需要进一步的分析。此外，SNS指标在不同类型的数据集和任务上的泛化能力也值得进一步探讨。

title: First-Token Broadcasters: Mechanistic Origins of Language Identity and Distributed Robustness in Transformers
comments: Linguistic Principles for Foundation Models (LP4FM) @ NeurIPS 2026
summary: How is language identity represented and causally maintained in transformers, and to what extent do the mechanisms identified in one language set transfer to other languages and training regimes? We introduce Language Identity Head Ablation (LIHA), a causal intervention that zeros each attention head individually and measures the resulting language switch rate. Across our multilingual evaluation sets, LIHA identifies heads whose ablation has disproportionate effects on output language. In GPT-2, a small set of first-token broadcaster heads---led by L6H1 (switch rate 0.32, 3.23$σ$ above the population mean)---attend persistently to the first prompt token across query positions. The combination of persistent first-token attention and causal sensitivity suggests that these heads participate in maintaining output language. Following ablation, first-token attention increases in heads above the ablated layer for the ablations tested (permutation test against random five-head sets, $p < 10^{-5}$). We do not test whether these heads functionally compensate for the ablated head. We also compare Qwen2.5-1.5B-Base and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, which are matched in architecture and parameter count but differ in training history. The base model is nearly flat (max SR$=$0.016, 200/336 heads at SR$=$0.0), whereas the instruct model concentrates causal influence at layer~0, led by L0H5 (SR$=$0.224, 8.93$σ$ above the mean). Finally, GPT-2 heads identified from the European-language experiments show no observed switch effects on the tested Chinese and Russian prompts, while other early-layer heads do show effects. Because script, typology, and tokenization vary together in this comparison, these results do not isolate a specifically script-driven mechanism. Repository is available at https://github.com/ajlrza/First-Token-Broadcasters.
